## 68. The Upcoming Flag

**Arena:** financial-market (listed apparel & footwear specialty retail equities, US + EU; market-neutral pairs plus earnings-dated options)
**Domain:** Apparel & fast fashion. RULES: institutions only; sanctioned collection

- **Data source:** The forward-dated fields inside affiliate-network PUBLISHER APIs — the retailer's own future markdown calendar, machine-readable, handed to approved affiliates before any consumer sees a discounted price. Three specific fields, all verified live in Awin's API docs today:

(1) Publisher Promotions API — `POST https://api.awin.com/publisher/{publisherId}/promotions` accepts a `status` filter whose documented values are "active", "expiringSoon", and **"upcoming" = "Offers which are not yet valid (their startDate is in the future)."** Response carries promotionId, type (promotion|voucher), advertiser{id,name,joined}, title, description, terms, **startDate, endDate (ISO-8601 UTC)**, dateAdded, regions, and voucher{code, exclusive, attributable}.

(2) Commission Groups API — `GET https://api.awin.com/publishers/{publisherId}/commissiongroups` returns per-advertiser groupName, groupCode, type (fix|percentage), amount/percentage, conditions, and critically **`ratesStart` — "ISO-8601 timestamp indicating when this set of rates becomes effective"** — plus `ratesEnd` and an `effectiveDate` query param for building history. A future `ratesStart` is a pre-announced change to the retailer's variable marketing spend.

(3) Publisher Product Feed — `GET https://api.awin.com/publishers/{PUBLISHER_ID}/awinfeeds/download/{ADVERTISER_ID}-retail-{LOCALE}`, JSONL, Google-format, documented to include regular price, **sale price with an effective date range**, availability (in stock / out of stock / preorder / backorder) plus availability date, GTIN, MPN, brand, size, color, gender, material, category. A `sale_price_effective_date` window that has not opened yet is a per-SKU scheduled markdown.

Same three primitives exist on CJ/Commission Junction (GraphQL Product Feed + Link Search promotional date fields), Rakuten Advertising (Coupon/Advertiser APIs), Impact.com, and Partnerize. Awin absorbed ShareASale (help.shareasale.com now 301s to help.awin.com), so one credential now spans a much larger US mid-cap apparel roster than it did two years ago.
- **How to collect it:** Stand up a real content/deals site, register as a publisher on Awin (+ShareASale), CJ, Rakuten Advertising, Impact.com and Partnerize, and get approved to the programs of ~80-150 listed apparel/footwear advertisers. Approval is per-advertiser and human-reviewed; budget 2-4 months and a plausible site. Cost: low thousands.

Then poll daily against api.awin.com (bearer token; 20 calls/min platform limit, 5/min on feeds):
- promotions with `status=upcoming` → forward markdown calendar per advertiser
- `/commissiongroups` daily, plus `effectiveDate` sweeps → detect any `ratesStart` in the future
- `awinfeeds/download/{advertiserId}-retail-{locale}` → nightly JSONL snapshot; diff SKU-level `sale_price` + its effective-date window + availability

Store immutable daily snapshots (the whole edge is the diff, so never overwrite). Per retailer per day compute: forward markdown breadth (% of catalog with a sale window opening in T+1..T+45), forward depth (mean discount off regular price on those SKUs), promo event count and exclusivity mix in the next 45 days vs. same calendar day last year, scheduled commission delta with its effective date, and out-of-stock rate by category/size (a bloat-vs-clean-inventory cross-check).

Docs verified: https://help.awin.com/apidocs/promotions.md, https://help.awin.com/apidocs/gets-an-array-of-commission-groups-for-an-advertiser.md, https://help.awin.com/apidocs/retail-publisher-productapidocumentation-1.md, https://help.awin.com/apidocs
- **The bet / trade:** Market-neutral basket inside apparel/footwear specialty retail, rebalanced on the fiscal calendar. Roughly 5 weeks before each name's quarter-end, rank the universe on (forward markdown breadth x depth for the final 4-5 weeks of the quarter, YoY) and on scheduled commission-rate direction. SHORT the 5-8 worst — biggest YoY jump in pre-scheduled discounting, especially those also showing a commission-rate CUT with a future `ratesStart`. LONG the 5-8 cleanest — flat/down forward promo with stable or rising commission. Hold through the earnings print, ~6-10 weeks, then flatten. Four cycles a year.

Universe: GAP, ANF, AEO, URBN, LULU, NKE, UAA, LEVI, VSCO, BOOT, JILL, DLTH, BKE, CURV, RVLV, KSS, M, DDS; EU leg HMB.ST, ZAL.DE, NXT.L, ASC.L, BOO.L.

Expression: cash equity pairs, or single-name shorts hedged with XRT. On the 2-3 highest-conviction shorts, buy earnings-cycle put spreads rather than outright puts — apparel IV into prints is rich, so sell the wing. Do not run naked shorts on the sub-$1bn names; borrow gets ugly.
- **Mechanism:** Apparel gross margin is, to a first approximation, one number: markdown rate. Everything else (freight, tariffs, cotton) moves slower and is better telegraphed.

The causal chain: a merchandising team decides in week N that a season has missed, and schedules the clearance. Executing that decision requires loading it into the promo calendar and the product feed *in advance*, because the whole downstream marketing stack — Google Shopping, cashback sites, coupon sites, editorial affiliates, email partners — needs lead time to build and schedule content. That is why the Google-format feed has a `sale_price_effective_date` window rather than just a price, why Awin's promotions API has an explicit `upcoming` status for offers whose startDate has not arrived, and why commission groups carry a `ratesStart` timestamp: publishers contractually need notice to re-forecast. None of this is a leak. It is required plumbing, and it is served over an authenticated API to a few thousand approved partners.

So the retailer publishes, dated and structured, the exact thing that determines next quarter's gross margin — before a single consumer sees a marked-down price tag. Deep + broad + early scheduled markdowns entering the last month of a quarter means the buyer has already conceded the season: margin miss now, plus inventory that carries into the following quarter, which is the part the market usually under-models.

The commission-rate field is the second, orthogonal signal and reads the CFO rather than the merchant. A scheduled cut in affiliate commission is variable customer-acquisition spend being pulled — it happens when CAC has outrun contribution margin, and it tends to precede a guide-down. The inverse (a rate rise plus a new-customer bonus group appearing) means they are buying revenue at the expense of margin: comps hold, margin doesn't. Either way you learn the direction of the trade-off before the print.
- **Who's on the other side:** Three groups, each slow for a different and durable reason.

1. Sell-side and long-only analysts run manual weekly "promo checks" — a human browsing gap.com on Thursday. They observe a discount the day it goes live, they observe depth but not schedule, and they sample maybe 30 SKUs. They are coincident and undersampled.

2. The price-scraping alt-data complex (EDITED, DataWeave, Yipit, Consumer Edge, Similarweb-adjacent shops). These crawl *rendered* product pages. A rendered page cannot show you a `sale_price_effective_date` window that has not opened, an offer sitting behind `status=upcoming`, or a `ratesStart` dated three weeks out. They are event-coincident by construction — not because they're lazy, but because the rendered DOM genuinely does not contain the future. This is the structural point: it is not a better scrape of the same surface, it is a different surface.

3. The people who actually see all of this every day — affiliate and performance-marketing operators at cashback and coupon companies — have no connection whatsoever to the buy side. This data lives in marketing-ops dashboards, read by people optimizing CPC and EPC. The information is sitting in plain sight in the wrong industry. That disconnect, not any technical difficulty, is the whole edge.
- **Information lead:** Differs by field, and honesty matters here because the trade lives or dies on it.

- Commission `ratesStart`: longest and hardest-dated. Advertisers typically schedule rate changes 2-6 weeks ahead because publishers require notice. This one is unambiguous — a timestamp in the future, sitting in a GET response.
- Promotions with `status=upcoming`: typically 3-21 days ahead for routine offers; 3-6 weeks for tentpole events (Black Friday, back-to-school, end-of-season clearance) where partners need long build times.
- `sale_price_effective_date` windows in the feed: usually 1-14 days before the window opens.

Versus the competition: days to weeks ahead of every price scraper and every analyst channel check, because they physically cannot see unexecuted schedules. Versus the market: you know the retailer's promotional posture for the final month of the quarter roughly a month before it executes, and 8-14 weeks before it shows up in a reported gross margin line. The tentpole-event lead is the most valuable slice — it is longest exactly when the quarter's margin is most at stake.
- **Why still under-exploited:** The moat is operational and legal, not technical — which is precisely the profile of a source that stays under-exploited for years.

(a) Access is gated by a human approval step, per merchant, per network. You must actually operate a credible publisher site and be individually accepted by each advertiser's affiliate manager. You cannot bulk-buy this, you cannot scrape around it, and a data vendor cannot industrialize it. It is slow, unglamorous relationship work that quant shops are structurally bad at.

(b) Network terms restrict *redistribution* of feeds and offers. That is exactly why no vendor packages and resells it — the business model is blocked. But using it yourself, as the publisher who was granted it, is the intended use. A source that is legal to collect and use internally but awkward to resell is one nobody converts into a product, so it never becomes consensus. This is the opposite of the Kpler/Vortexa/YipitData shape.

(c) The forward-dated fields are invisible plumbing. `status=upcoming`, `ratesStart`, `sale_price_effective_date` are boring integration details nobody in finance has ever read. The entire alt-data industry standardized on crawling rendered pages a decade ago and never revisited the assumption that the rendered page is the best available surface.

(d) It just got materially better: Awin's absorption of ShareASale (help.shareasale.com now redirects to help.awin.com) consolidated a large US mid-cap apparel roster behind one credential and one API, and the JSONL feed endpoint is recent. The surface area is bigger and cleaner than it was two years ago, and nobody has re-scoped it.

(e) Honest caveat on novelty: "promo tracking" as a category is thoroughly mined. The claim here is narrow and specific — not that discount tracking is new, but that the *scheduled, not-yet-live* layer is a distinct dataset with a real clock on it, reachable only through permissioned publisher APIs.
- **Rough +EV:** Deliberately unromantic. Apparel specialty retail earnings moves average ~8-12% absolute, and gross-margin surprise explains most of the reaction — so the payoff per event is large if you get direction right.

Assume the signal is real but noisy: 57-61% directional hit rate on a market-neutral pair, ~4-6% average absolute pair move over a 6-10 week hold. That is roughly +0.6-1.2% expected per pair. Running 8-15 pairs a quarter across US and EU gives ~4-9% annual gross on deployed capital at low net exposure.

Costs bite hard: borrow on small-cap apparel shorts runs 2-8% annualized and occasionally far worse on crowded names, plus slippage in thin mid-caps. Realistic net is low-to-mid single digits standalone, Sharpe maybe 0.6-1.0. Setup is a few thousand dollars and 2-4 months of approvals — cheap relative to the option value.

The better-shaped version of this trade is probably not standalone: use it as a veto/confirm overlay on apparel positions you already hold, and to size earnings-dated put spreads on the 2-3 names where forward markdown depth is most extreme. Concentrating the signal where it is strongest, rather than diluting across a full basket, is where the risk-adjusted return actually is. It fires ~4x/year per name, so this is a patient, calendar-driven strategy, not a high-turnover one.
- **Confidence:** Medium.

Biggest uncertainty, stated plainly: I have verified the API *contracts* — the `upcoming` status filter, the `ratesStart` timestamp, and the sale-price effective-date range all provably exist and provably carry future dates. What I have NOT measured is the empirical distribution of lead times per retailer. If the median large US apparel retailer loads its promotions at T-1 rather than T-14, the lead collapses toward zero and this degenerates into an expensive, permissioned re-derivation of what price scrapers already sell. Everything rests on that distribution.

The saving grace is that this is cheap and fast to falsify before risking capital: join ~20 programs, log the three endpoints daily for 60 days, and directly measure the lead-time distribution per advertiser. Retailers will sort into "schedules ahead" (tradeable) and "same-day" (useless), and you simply run the strategy only on the former. Do that measurement before committing a dollar of risk.

Secondary risks, in rough order: (1) selection bias — affiliate-visible promos over-represent coupon-code offers and may under-represent in-store and unadvertised clearance, so the feed measures a slice of markdown activity rather than all of it; (2) approval rejection by precisely the premium brands you most want, since some reject non-editorial publishers; (3) CJ's docs are a JS SPA I could not render, so my claim that CJ/Rakuten/Impact carry equivalent forward-dated fields is inference from the shared Google-feed standard rather than direct verification — Awin is the only network I confirmed field-by-field; (4) network terms constrain redistribution, so this must stay an internal research input.

## 69. The 00145 Print

**Arena:** financial-market
**Domain:** Grocery & CPG. RULES: institutions only; sanctioned collection

- **Data source:** EPA NPDES Discharge Monitoring Report (DMR) data for food-manufacturing plants — specifically parameter code 00145 "Total production - mass" (reported in lb/day), plus 50050 Flow (MGD), 00310 BOD5 (mg/L and lb/day loading), 00530 TSS and 00556 Oil & Grease. Federal effluent guidelines for the food sector (40 CFR Parts 405-432: dairy, grain mills, canned/preserved fruits & vegetables, meat & poultry, seafood) set production-NORMALIZED limits, so permittees are legally required to self-report actual plant production every month in order to demonstrate compliance. This is not a proxy — it is the plant's own monthly output number, filed with a regulator and published free. Second tier: for plants that discharge to a municipal sewer rather than surface water, the equivalent Significant Industrial User self-monitoring reports sit with the local POTW pretreatment Control Authority, and CWA Sec. 308(b) / 40 CFR 2.302 expressly deny confidential treatment to effluent data, so they must be released on request. Third tier, free bonus: construction stormwater permits expose codenamed capacity projects before capex is disclosed.
- **How to collect it:** All verified live on 2026-08-14 via the ECHO REST API (no key, no login). (1) Map company to permits: https://echodata.epa.gov/echo/cwa_rest_services.get_facilities?output=JSON&p_fn=LAMB%20WESTON then get_qid?qid=NNN. Confirmed 16 Lamb Weston records, 9 Freshpet records, 8 Vital Farms records. (2) Screen the universe: same endpoint with p_ncs=311&p_majflag=Y returns 2,295 major food-manufacturing CWA facilities nationally. (3) Pull the numbers: https://echodata.epa.gov/echo/eff_rest_services.get_effluent_chart?output=JSON&p_id=<PERMIT>&start_date=01/01/2025&end_date=08/14/2026 returns PermFeatures -> Parameters -> DischargeMonitoringReports with MonitoringPeriodEndDate and DMRValueNmbr. Confirmed real values: AMERICAS CATCH INC (MS) param 00145 = 135,845 and 231,497 lb/d for Jan-2024; C F GOLLOTT & SON SEAFOOD (MS) 40,679 lb/d Feb-24, 16,173 Mar-24, 88,798 May-24. 29 of 48 sampled food permits returned numeric data. (4) Bulk history: ECHO Water Pollutant Loading Tool downloads at https://echo.epa.gov/trends/loading-tool/get-data. (5) For POTW dischargers, ECHO tags them with "PIU" SourceIDs (e.g. Freshpet Bethlehem = PAPIU00FR) — that tells you exactly which city pretreatment office to send the Sec. 308(b) records request to. Total build: one engineer, a few weeks, mostly spent hand-building the permit-to-subsidiary-to-ticker crosswalk.
- **The bet / trade:** Directional single-name equity or short-dated call/put spreads into quarterly earnings on plant-concentrated, foodservice/B2B-weighted US food manufacturers. Flagship: Lamb Weston (LW) — a near-pure-play frozen potato processor whose earnings variance is almost entirely plant volume and capacity utilization, and which has repeatedly gapped 15-20% on volume. Supporting book: Freshpet (FRPT, two-kitchen network at Bethlehem PA and Ennis TX, entire bull case is line yield and throughput), Vital Farms (VITL, Egg Central Station plus the new Seymour IN plant), B&G Foods (BGS). Direction set by the effluent-derived production nowcast versus consensus volume; enter roughly 2-3 weeks before the print once two of the three months in the quarter are in hand, hold through the report. Horizon 3-6 weeks. Also a slower capex trade: a new construction-stormwater permit under a codename (verified: "FRESHPET PHASE 2A" TXR1512UN in Ennis TX; "PROJECT TRIDENT" ORR10F185 in Hermiston OR, a Lamb Weston site) front-runs the capacity-expansion announcement by quarters.
- **Mechanism:** Food processing is water-intensive and the wastewater load is close to mechanically proportional to physical throughput: potatoes washed, birds chilled, eggs washed, meat cooked. Because the federal effluent guidelines express limits as pounds of pollutant per 1,000 pounds of raw material processed, the permittee cannot compute its own compliance without disclosing production — so monthly output lands in a public regulatory database as a side effect of environmental law. Chain: plant runs more pounds -> higher reported 00145 production, higher flow, higher BOD/FOG loading -> aggregate across a company's permitted plants -> quarterly volume -> revenue and, critically, gross margin, because these are high-fixed-cost plants where utilization drives the margin bridge. The second-order signal is the sharper one: water and BOD per pound of output is an inverse yield proxy. If loading rises faster than shipped volume, the plant is running short campaigns, more clean-in-place changeovers and off-spec product — i.e. yield is deteriorating and the gross margin bridge will miss even if the volume line looks fine. A new line commissioning shows up as a step change in flow weeks before the company confirms it is running at rate.
- **Who's on the other side:** Long-only food/staples funds and sell-side analysts who model volume from retail scanner panels (Circana, NielsenIQ, Numerator) and card panels, plus the market makers pricing earnings straddles. They are structurally wrong here rather than merely slow: scanner and card data observe the SHELF, and every mainstream alt-data product — YipitData, M Science, Similarweb, satellite parking counts — is built on consumer-facing signals. Lamb Weston sells the large majority of its volume into foodservice and QSR distribution; Freshpet's throughput question is inside its own kitchens; private-label and co-packer volume never appears under a measurable brand at all. None of that is visible in retail POS. So for exactly the names where volume is the whole debate, the entire commercial alt-data complex is blind, and the sell-side is reduced to reasoning from management's last guide. Effluent data looks at the factory instead of the shelf, which is the one place nobody is looking.
- **Information lead:** Real and measurable. I confirmed on 2026-08-14 that July 2026 monitoring-period values were already published for the fastest filers (Alyeska Seafoods Unalaska: BOD 4,866 mg/L and 65,706 lb/d, TSS, pH) — roughly a two-week lag from month end. Typical NetDMR filers land 30-45 days after the monitoring period, with a weekly ECHO refresh. Against a company that reports a quarter 5-7 weeks after it closes, that yields about 8-12 weeks of lead on the first month of a quarter, 4-8 weeks on the second, and usually the full quarter 1-3 weeks before the print. Because most of the surprise variance in these names is a volume or utilization break that shows up early in the quarter, having months 1 and 2 cleanly in hand is where the edge actually lives. The codenamed construction-permit signal leads disclosed capex by one to three quarters.
- **Why still under-exploited:** Nobody sells this and the obstacles are unglamorous rather than technical. (1) The data is keyed by NPDES permit ID, not by ticker; the value is entirely in a hand-built permit-to-subsidiary-to-parent crosswalk, and the names are messy — Lamb Weston's plants are still filed under "CONAGRA FOODS LAMB WESTON" a decade after the spin. (2) The gold parameter is a five-digit code (00145) buried among thousands of water-quality codes, meaningful only if you know the effluent guidelines force production disclosure — that is environmental-compliance knowledge, not finance knowledge. (3) Coverage is genuinely fragmented, which repels productizers: I verified some plants are rich (Richland WA, 166 monthly values), some are empty legacy "Unpermitted Facility" stubs, and POTW dischargers like Freshpet Bethlehem show a live individual permit with zero values in ECHO because the actual reports live at the city pretreatment office and must be requested one municipality at a time. (4) Environmental datasets are culturally coded as ESG-screening or litigation material, so quant shops that have scraped ECHO used it to flag violations, not to nowcast output. The manual, per-city, per-permit grind is exactly what keeps it out of a vendor's catalog and available to a small team.
- **Rough +EV:** Fires on maybe 12-20 usable earnings events a year — roughly 8-12 names with adequate plant coverage, minus the quarters where the data is too sparse to take a view. Base rate on volume direction into a print for a well-covered name should be around 60-65% versus a coin flip, since you are reading two-thirds of the quarter's actual production. These names carry 8-15% average absolute earnings-day moves, so an equity position sized on a confident read is worth roughly 3-6% expected return per event, more with short-dated spreads where the straddle is priced off a genuinely uninformed distribution. A focused book running 12-18 events a year should target something like +8-18% annualized on deployed capital, front-loaded into the two or three quarters a year where the nowcast disagrees sharply with consensus and the position deserves real size. The codenamed-capex leg is lower frequency but occasionally a large, slow multi-quarter winner. Costs are near zero — the API is free and unmetered; the real cost is the crosswalk build and periodic records requests.
- **Confidence:** Medium. The data unambiguously exists, is fresh, is free, and is legally protected from confidentiality claims — I pulled real production numbers in lb/day and July 2026 values in mid-August 2026. The biggest uncertainty is coverage-to-materiality mapping: verified directly that Lamb Weston's richest permit (Richland WA) reports temperature and conductivity but not production, that several of its records are empty legacy stubs, and that Freshpet's Bethlehem permit shows zero values in ECHO because it is a pretreatment industrial user whose reports sit with the city. So for any given ticker, the permitted plants you can actually read may cover too little of total output to constrain the quarter — the honest first step is a coverage audit that scores each name on percent-of-capacity observable, and simply passing on the ones that score low. Secondary risks: effluent load is contaminated by clean-in-place sanitation and rainfall infiltration, so it is noisier than a pure throughput meter; state-run programs vary in how completely they push DMRs into ICIS; and for a foodservice-weighted name, plant production leads shipments by an inventory-build term you have to estimate separately.

## 70. The Presale Bond

**Arena:** financial-market
**Domain:** Gyms, fitness & wellness. RULES: institutions only; sanctioned collection

- **Data source:** State health-spa/health-club consumer-protection registries — specifically the Texas Secretary of State Health Spa registry (Tex. Occ. Code Ch. 702), which is a per-location, weekly-refreshed census of every gym in Texas with the owning franchisee LLC named, a status field (Active / Registration Ended / Expired / Rejected / Closed Final), an annual expiration date, a surety company, a security-posted-vs-EXEMPT flag, and a registration number encoded as YYYYnnnn (issue-year vintage). Because §702.101 forbids operating OR offering/selling a membership without a certificate, and §702.352 forces an escrow filing (Form 3005) within 14 days of the first prepayment on a not-yet-open club, the registry is populated by gyms that have signed a lease and started presales but have not opened. The security amount is tiered by the location's total prepaid membership dollars ($20k floor stepping to $50k above $45k of prepaid memberships) — a coarse per-location prepaid-revenue disclosure. Companion registries exist in Virginia (VDACS Office of Charitable and Regulatory Programs), Florida (FDACS Health Studios, Ch. 501 Pt. XI), Ohio (AG prepaid entertainment contracts), and Tennessee.
- **How to collect it:** Three free, sanctioned pulls, no scraping-hostile terms: (1) the weekly full census PDF at https://www.sos.state.tx.us/statdoc/healthspas/healthspas.pdf — "Currently Active Health Spas as of 8/12/2026," 88 pages, ~2,200 locations, columns HEALTH SPA / ADDRESS / CITY / STATE / ZIP / SECURITY(YES|EXEMPT); the page states it is refreshed every Wednesday, so you diff snapshots week over week. (2) the classic-ASP search at https://direct.sos.state.tx.us/healthspas/HSsearch.asp — POST form fields Reg_No, DBA_Name, PhysicalAddress, City, ZC, RegistrantName, RegistrantAddress, RegCity, RegState, RegZC, ssubmit=All (vs. Active). A single POST of DBA_Name="PLANET FITNESS" returns 279 records including dead ones: 217 Active, 33 Registration Ended, 18 Rejected, 10 Expired, 1 Closed Final — which means the entire multi-year history backfills today, no waiting to accumulate snapshots. Registration-number vintages parse straight out to a gross-registration time series (TX Planet Fitness: 2022=27, 2023=9, 2024=37, 2025=16, 2026 YTD=11). (3) the Health Spa Closings bulletin on https://www.sos.state.tx.us/statdoc/healthspas/index.shtml, where SOS publicly names closed clubs so members can claim against the security (currently naming e.g. UFCGym Pearland; LA Fitness & Pro Results Pasadena). Cross-state: https://www.vdacs.virginia.gov/pdf/health-club-status.pdf (Virginia's registered-club list with per-location expiry, 20pp, verified), FDACS ConsumerCompliance portal for Florida. Total build: a few hundred lines of Python plus pypdf; the whole Texas panel is under 2 MB/week.
- **The bet / trade:** Primary: Planet Fitness (PLNT) equity, direction set by the signal, entered 2-4 weeks before fiscal quarter-end and held through the earnings print roughly 5-6 weeks after quarter-end — a 6-10 week hold; expressed in options as slightly-OTM calls or puts spanning the print when IV allows. Two distinct triggers with opposite signs. SHORT trigger: a registrant-entity cascade in the weekly diff — multiple locations under one franchisee LLC flipping Active to Registration Ended/Expired in the same or consecutive weeks, a jump in Rejected applications, an EXEMPT location newly forced to post security (loss of the §702.202 exemption requires that no closure/failure-to-open complaint has been filed against the certificate holder, so losing it is a filed-complaint tell), or brand locations appearing on the Closings bulletin. LONG trigger: acceleration in freshly issued 2026-series registration numbers plus new Form 3005 escrow filings, both of which only exist for clubs already collecting presale money at unopened sites. Secondary expressions: Life Time (LTH) equity, and for credit desks the Planet Fitness Master Issuer whole-business securitization notes and the term loans of Crunch (82 TX locations registered), EoS (38), Gold's (78), and Purpose Brands/Anytime Fitness (305) + Orangetheory (130).
- **Mechanism:** Texas law makes the state registry a mandatory, dated waypoint on the physical path a gym takes from lease to open door to failure. A club cannot legally take the first presale dollar without a certificate on file, and if it takes prepayments before opening it must file escrow paperwork within 14 days. So every unit in the opening pipeline has to surface in the registry months before it shows up in a franchisor's unit count. On the way down, the same statute forces disclosure in reverse: the certificate is annual, non-renewal shows as Registration Ended, and because the security deposit exists to pay members burned by a closure, the SOS publishes closings by name so claims can be filed. The registrant field is the load-bearing part — it names the franchisee LLC, not the brand. Planet Fitness in Texas is essentially entirely franchised, and the registry cleanly resolves the large multi-unit operators (United PF entities hold 24+ registrations, Excel Fitness entities another dozen-plus across DFW). PLNT's earnings and, more importantly, its forward opening guidance are a direct function of whether those franchisee groups have the balance sheet and appetite to keep building. Franchisee credit stress shows up first as stalled/rejected new registrations and lapsed certificates on marginal units, quarters before it shows up as a guidance cut. The security ladder adds a second channel: a location's required deposit is set by its total prepaid membership dollars, so bond tier migration is a crude same-store prepaid-revenue read that nobody has ever mapped.
- **Who's on the other side:** Sell-side analysts who model PLNT unit growth by taking company guidance and applying a haircut — they have no independent pre-opening observable and no franchisee-level view at all. The alt-data incumbents are structurally blind here rather than merely slow: geolocation panels (Placer.ai, Advan, Veraset) count visits to places that already exist, cannot see a club that has not opened, and cannot distinguish a closed club from a slow week for months; card panels (Yipit, M Science, Consumer Edge) see the brand descriptor on the transaction, not the franchisee LLC, so a specific operator's portfolio rolling over is invisible to them. FRANdata is the closest competitor and works from annual FDDs and franchise agreements — a once-a-year, self-reported, lagged view. Index and passive flow is the residual buyer. On the credit side, ratings analysts on the WBS notes get monthly servicer reports of system sales, which already embed the outcome the registry predicted.
- **Information lead:** New units: registration must precede any membership sale, and presale windows on this format run roughly 4-10 weeks before doors open, with registrations often filed earlier — so you see a unit 1-4 months before it opens, and the opening only reaches the tape in a quarterly report filed ~5-6 weeks after quarter-end. Net lead on the reported number: 2-6 months. Closures: an Active-to-Registration-Ended flip or a name on the Closings bulletin is visible within days on the Wednesday refresh, versus 6 weeks to 4 months before the net unit count is disclosed. Franchisee distress: a registrant-entity cascade or a lost security exemption typically precedes any public commentary on franchisee health by 1-3 quarters. And the Rejected status — an application that never converted — is a failed-site signal that literally never appears in any company disclosure at all.
- **Why still under-exploited:** This is a 1990s consumer-protection artifact filed under "Statutory Documents Section," sitting next to athlete agents and credit services organizations, and nobody in finance reads it as a business dataset. There is no API, no bulk export, no CSV, no vendor product — the delivery mechanisms are an 88-page weekly PDF and a classic-ASP form that renders results as unstructured text blocks rather than a table (I had to reconstruct records by walking label sequences, not by parsing rows). The value is fragmented across states with wholly incompatible regimes: Texas SOS, Virginia VDACS, Florida FDACS, Ohio AG, Tennessee SOS, each with its own definition, exemption carve-outs, and publication format, so building national coverage is a per-state manual slog with no reusable schema. The registrant-to-franchisee mapping — the single most valuable field — requires entity-resolving hundreds of shell LLCs ("Excel Fitness DFW XVI, LLC") back to parent operators. That combination of ugly delivery, statutory obscurity, and per-state fragmentation is exactly why it has stayed clean while foot-traffic and card panels got commoditized.
- **Rough +EV:** Fires 5-7 actionable times a year: four earnings events with a directional tilt, plus 1-3 franchisee-distress cascades. Be honest about the nowcast half — Texas is ~217 of PLNT's ~2,700 US locations (~8%), so a 3-5 unit quarterly TX count is a sampling-noisy read on a ~35-45 unit national number, and TX skews Sun Belt growth, meaning it will systematically overstate the national opening rate. You trade the change versus Texas's own history, never the level. Realistic directional hit rate on the earnings tilt: 56-62%, against typical 8-15% PLNT earnings moves, so ~1.5-3.5% expected per event on deployed capital. The real money is the distress tail, which is a step function rather than a noisy count: a top-franchisee cascade caught a quarter early against a mid-cap that has repeatedly gapped on franchisee-health scares is a 10-20% capture, and those are the events where the other side has literally no instrument. Blended expectation for the sleeve: ~8-15% gross annually, heavily skewed to two or three trades, before costs. Marginal cost of running it is near zero — a weekly PDF diff and a few hundred POSTs.
- **Confidence:** Medium. The data source is fully verified — I pulled the live 88-page Texas census (dated 8/12/2026, ~2,200 locations with the YES/EXEMPT security flag), executed a working search POST returning 279 Planet Fitness records with the status taxonomy and franchisee entities intact, confirmed the statutory pre-sale registration and 14-day escrow requirements in the SOS FAQ, and confirmed Virginia's parallel list. The biggest uncertainty is registration-timing hygiene: the statute compels registration before the first membership sale, but operators may file in batches, file late, or register a location well ahead of a lease that later dies (the 18 Rejected records prove some of the pipeline is vapor), which would smear the lead and inject false positives into the opening signal. That is testable before risking capital — the backfillable panel of expired records plus registration-number vintages lets you reconstruct several years of TX registrations today and regress them against PLNT's actually-reported Texas openings, which is the first thing to do and the thing that would kill or confirm the idea. The secondary uncertainty is whether an 8% single-state sample carries enough national signal on the count side; my honest read is that it does not carry the level but does carry the second derivative and the distress tail, which is where I would concentrate the risk.

## 71. The Infant Seat Ledger

**Arena:** financial-market (US equities: KLC, BFAM — single-name equity and short-dated post-earnings options)
**Domain:** Childcare, senior care & healthcare facilities. RULES: institutions only; sanctioned collection

- **Data source:** Per-center, AGE-BAND licensed capacity and license-status fields inside state child care licensing registries — specifically the infant/toddler seat counts, the `temporarily_closed` / `Suspended` / `Pending Revocation` / `adverse_action` flags, and new-license issuance dates and street addresses, for every center legally operated by KinderCare (KLC) and Bright Horizons (BFAM). This is NOT the well-known "count the licensed centers" exercise: the tradeable variable is the age-band mix within a fixed total capacity, because infant seats carry ~1.5–2x the tuition of preschool seats (1:3–1:5 mandated ratios vs 1:10–1:15) and are the binding constraint on both revenue-per-child and staffing. Two centers with identical `total_capacity` of 150 have entirely different revenue capacity depending on infant seats. Verified live: NY OCFS carries `infant_capacity`/`toddler_capacity`/`preschool_capacity`/`school_age_capacity` per center; CO CDEC carries `licensed_infant_capacity` etc.; TX HHSC carries `total_capacity` plus a daily `temporarily_closed` boolean and `adverse_action`.
- **How to collect it:** All official government open-data APIs, public domain, documented, no auth, no ToS issue. Verified working this session: (1) NY OCFS — https://data.ny.gov/resource/cb42-qumz.json (Socrata SoQL; `$where=upper(facility_name) like '%KINDERCARE%' OR upper(facility_name) like '%BRIGHT HORIZONS%'`); rowsUpdatedAt 2026-08-14 04:17 UTC — updated within the hour; returned 41 KLC/BFAM facilities with full age-band capacity and statuses including `Suspended`, `Pending Revocation and Denial`. (2) TX HHSC CCL Operations — https://data.texas.gov/resource/bc5r-88dy.json (updated 2026-08-13); returned 74 KinderCare operations, 10,808 total seats, with `temporarily_closed`, `adverse_action`, `deficiency_high`, `accepts_child_care_subsidies`, `issuance_date`. (3) TX HHSC Non-Compliance — https://data.texas.gov/resource/tqgd-mf4x.json (daily), citation-level with `standard_number_description`, `standard_risk_level`, and a free-text `narrative` that frequently records children and staff physically present at inspection — the regulator literally counting the room. Join to (2) on `operation_id`. (4) CO CDEC — https://data.colorado.gov/resource/a9rr-k8mu.json (monthly, updated 2026-08-04), per-center `licensed_infant_capacity`/`toddler`/`preschool`/`school_age`. (5) PA https://data.pa.gov/resource/ajn5-kaxt.json (daily), WA https://data.wa.gov/resource/was8-3ni8.json, CT https://data.ct.gov/resource/6rnk-h6iy.json, DE https://data.delaware.gov/resource/wb83-pkcv.json. Discover more via the federated Socrata catalog: https://api.us.socrata.com/api/catalog/v1?q=child+care+licens. Remaining big states (CA CCLD, FL DCF, OH, IL, NC DCDEE, GA DECAL, MI LARA, AZ DHS) require light scraping of their public licensing-search portals. CRITICAL MECHANIC: every one of these states OVERWRITES the current snapshot rather than archiving it (Colorado's explicit time-series file froze in 2019). No history exists unless you snapshot nightly and diff. A cron job storing daily JSON per state plus a diff table on (center_id, age_band_capacity, status) is the entire pipeline — one small VM. Entity resolution is the real work: name strings are filthy ("KinderCare Learning Centers LLC", "Castle Rock Kindercare", "Cordera Kindercare Learning Center", "Knowledge Learning Corporation", "CCLC", "Bright Horizons Children's Center @20 Pine"), so match on address geocode plus fuzzy name against the company center locator.
- **The bet / trade:** Primary: KLC (KinderCare Learning Companies) equity, direction conditional on the signal, accumulated intra-quarter and held through the earnings print — roughly a 60–90 day hold. Go long when the diffed panel shows net infant/toddler seat additions, falling `temporarily_closed`/`adverse_action` counts, and net new license issuances; fade/short when infant seats are being converted out, temporary-closure counts are climbing, or enforcement statuses are accumulating. Express the high-conviction cases in short-dated calls/puts spanning the report date, since KLC's earnings-day distribution is fat. Secondary: run BFAM as the paired offset to strip out sector/rate beta, and take the BFAM employer-campus tape as a standalone long/short overlay — a new BFAM license appearing at a corporate campus address is a client win 2–6 months before it is disclosed; a lapse at a client campus is a client loss BFAM will not volunteer. Settlement: the quarterly print of same-center enrollment/occupancy and center count.
- **Mechanism:** Childcare center revenue is capacity mix, not capacity. Infant rooms are the highest-price, highest-margin, most staff-intensive product; preschool rooms are the cheapest to staff. Since the post-pandemic labor squeeze, the industry's binding constraint flipped from demand to teacher supply, and the operator's rational response to not being able to staff an infant room is to re-band it — legally converting infant seats to preschool seats, or shuttering the room. That re-banding is not a private management decision: it requires a license amendment filed with the state, which lands in the public registry as a changed integer in `infant_capacity`. So the causal chain is: local teacher labor tightens or demand shifts -> operator amends the license -> registry integer changes (observable within days in TX/NY/PA) -> weeks-to-months later the effect shows up in reported revenue-per-child, same-center enrollment and occupancy -> the stock reprices on the print. The status flags run the same chain faster and harder: a `temporarily_closed` flip or an `adverse_action` is an immediate, total revenue outage at that center, visible the day the state posts it. For BFAM the mechanism is different and cleaner — its centers are employer-sponsored and physically sited at client campuses, so the registry's street-address field is a direct read on the client roster, and license issuance necessarily precedes center opening.
- **Who's on the other side:** A very thin sell-side bench (roughly 5–8 analysts across KLC and BFAM) modeling almost entirely off management guidance and commentary, plus BLS CES "child day care services" national employment — which is monthly, national, and has zero operator granularity. Foot-traffic vendors (Placer.ai and similar) are structurally poor here: childcare dwell times are short, centers are residential-adjacent and constantly mis-attributed, and the panels cannot distinguish an infant drop-off from a preschool one, which is the entire signal. Long-only holders and the Partners Group post-IPO overhang are on the other side of flow. They are slow for a structural reason rather than a lazy one: the information is genuinely expensive to assemble — 50 incompatible schemas and ID systems, filthy operator name strings, and no vendor selling the assembled panel — so it sits below every institutional research budget's threshold while remaining trivially affordable for one determined person with a cron job.
- **Information lead:** Very large and continuous. TX, NY and PA repost daily (NY's file was written minutes before I queried it); CO monthly. KLC reports roughly 5–6 weeks after quarter end. So a re-banding or closure occurring in week 2 of a quarter is observable within days and is not disclosed for approximately 16–18 weeks — a 6–14 week lead depending on where in the quarter the event lands, and, more importantly, a continuous read where the market gets four discrete snapshots a year. The BFAM client-win lead is longer still: license issuance precedes center opening by roughly 2–6 months and precedes any disclosure by longer, if it is ever disclosed at a center level at all. The overwrite mechanic converts this lead into a compounding moat — every night you snapshot and your competitors do not, your history gets longer and theirs stays at zero, and the states will not sell them the back file because it no longer exists.
- **Why still under-exploited:** No commercial product assembles it. The alternative-data majors sell card panels, foot traffic, web scrapes and shipping — none sells a center-level childcare licensing panel, because the addressable market is two public tickers and the assembly cost is high relative to that. Four reinforcing reasons it stays that way: (1) fragmentation — only about 8–10 states expose clean Socrata APIs, the rest need bespoke portal scraping, and every state uses a different ID system and age-band definition; (2) entity resolution is genuinely manual, since the operator name strings are inconsistent even within a single state file; (3) no history exists to backtest against, because states overwrite rather than archive — Colorado's own time-series attempt died in 2019 — so the standard quant workflow of "buy history, backtest, deploy" is impossible and the only path is to start collecting and wait, which institutional research processes are badly built for; (4) attention collapse — childcare data drew a burst of interest during the ARPA stabilization-funds story and was abandoned when that ended, and KLC has only been public since October 2024, so no one has had either the reason or the elapsed time to build the panel. The age-band insight specifically is the under-exploited part: the handful of people who have looked at these registries at all counted centers, which companies disclose anyway, rather than looking inside the center at the seat mix, which they do not.
- **Rough +EV:** Modest but real, and it compounds. Realistic clean coverage is 30–45% of the KLC US footprint from the API states at launch, rising toward 60–70% once CA/FL/OH/IL/NC/GA scrapers are added. On the directional call for whether same-center enrollment/occupancy surprises above or below consensus, I would estimate a 58–62% hit rate against a 50% baseline — the edge is concentrated at the extremes (closure waves, enforcement clusters, infant-room elimination programs) and is close to nil for ordinary enrollment drift. KLC's earnings-day absolute move is plausibly 8–15%. Sizing a moderate position four times a year per name, plus the BFAM pair and the client-win overlay, nets roughly 150–400 bps of edge per event before costs, call it 6–15% annualized on capital deployed in this sleeve. The fat tail is the one that pays for the whole effort: catching a multi-state closure or adverse-action wave three months before it is disclosed is a single-event move worth more than several years of the base signal, and the daily flags are exactly what surfaces it. Costs are negligible — one small VM, free APIs — so the strategy is capacity-constrained by the tickers' liquidity, not by data spend.
- **Confidence:** Medium. The data is verified live and unambiguous — I pulled current rows from NY, TX and CO this session and confirmed named KLC/BFAM centers with populated age-band capacity, daily update stamps, and live enforcement statuses — so source risk is essentially zero. The biggest uncertainty is squarely the mechanism, not the data: licensed capacity is a legal ceiling, not enrollment. KLC runs somewhere around 70% occupancy, which means a center can lose 15% of its children with no registry change whatsoever, and conversely an operator can leave an infant room licensed but unstaffed and dark for a full quarter. So the signal is strong for discrete events (closures, temporary closures, adverse actions, formal re-bandings) and genuinely weak for the ordinary enrollment drift that drives most quarters — and I cannot pre-validate the elasticity between seat-mix deltas and reported revenue-per-child because the historical panel does not exist to backtest. That is the honest crux: this idea requires you to start collecting and run it forward for two or three quarters before you know the coefficient. Secondary uncertainties are partial and geographically skewed state coverage, and the risk that re-banding amendments turn out to be rarer and more sluggish than the labor-market story implies, which would leave only the status flags carrying the signal.

## 72. The Counselor Roster (Addendum A)

**Arena:** financial-market — US equities and equity options (deathcare consolidators: SCI, CSV)
**Domain:** Death care & actuarial. RULES: institutions only; sanctioned collection

- **Data source:** "Addendum A — Preneed Sales Agents, Clean Applications," a PDF buried inside the monthly agenda packet of the Florida Board of Funeral, Cemetery and Consumer Services (Florida Dept. of Financial Services). Under Fla. Stat. 497.466, every preneed sales agent in Florida must be individually licensed AND appointed to a specific preneed licensee. Addendum A publishes, every month, the full named roster of newly licensed agents with the column "Appointing Entity Name" — i.e., the employer. Verified in the 7/23/2026 packet: 13 new agents appointed to SCI FUNERAL SERVICES OF FLORIDA LLC (AE# 115439), 2 to CARRIAGE FLORIDA HOLDINGS INC, 1 to FPG FLORIDA LLC (Foundation Partners), plus columns for PSA Original Issue Date and PSA Appointment Date (which separate true new hires from poached/transferred agents). This is a monthly, employer-attributed headcount feed for the deathcare preneed salesforce — a metric SCI itself no longer discloses. The same packet carries two free bonus series: (a) the "Administrative Report" level counts (Active Sales Agents = 3,775 as of 7/14/2026; Active Preneed Licenses = 302; Cemetery Acquisition Applications pending), and (b) named M&A items — the 7/23/2026 agenda item Q(2)(a) reads "SCI Funeral Services of Florida LLC — Application to Acquire Control of an Existing Cemetery Company; Application for Transfer of Preneed License," an unannounced acquisition sitting in plain sight. Archive runs monthly back to 2007 (~220 observations), giving a real backtest sample.
- **How to collect it:** Fully sanctioned public-meeting material under Florida's Sunshine Law; no scraping of anything gated. (1) Scrape the link list at https://www.myfloridacfo.com/division/funeralcemetery/board/board-agendas (plus /board-agenda-archive for 2007-2024). (2) Each meeting has an agenda PDF (e.g. .../board-agendas-2026/agenda_7-23-26.pdf) and an addenda ZIP (.../addenda-2026/addenda_7-23-26.zip). (3) Unzip; the file "D. Preneed Sales Agent - Addendum A.pdf" is the roster. Text-extract with pdfminer.six (rows key off the AE#+PSA-license pair, regex `(\d{6}) (F\d{6})`). (4) Map appointing entities to public issuers: SCI = "SCI FUNERAL SERVICES OF FLORIDA LLC" + "NEPTUNE MANAGEMENT CORP" (Neptune Society/Trident, SCI-owned); CSV = "CARRIAGE FLORIDA HOLDINGS INC"; private comps FPG FLORIDA LLC (Foundation Partners), NORTHSTAR CEMETERY SERVICES OF FLORIDA LLC, LEGACY FUNERAL HOLDINGS OF FLORIDA. (5) Cross-check the level and terminations against the DFS public licensee search (licenseesearch.fldfs.com). Verified working series of SCI gross adds/month: Feb-25=26, Sep-25=13, Dec-25=22, Mar-26=19, Apr-26=22, Jun-26=42, Jul-26=13 (SCI+Neptune combined). Total pull is ~250 ZIPs, roughly two hours of one person's time; ongoing cost is one cron job per month. Replicate in TX (Dept. of Banking prepaid funeral permits) and CA (Cemetery & Funeral Bureau) to widen coverage.
- **The bet / trade:** Primary: long Service Corporation International (NYSE: SCI) — common plus 90-150 day slightly OTM calls spanning the next TWO quarterly prints — when the 3-month rolling z-score of SCI-entity net counselor adds in Florida exceeds +1.5σ (the June 2026 packet at 42 adds vs. a ~16/month baseline is exactly this trigger). Reverse it — short-dated puts or a paired short vs. an equal-weight consumer-staples basket — when net adds run negative for two consecutive packets. Horizon: 4-7 months, exit after the second earnings report covering the ramped cohort. Secondary, higher-torque leg: when a named "Application to Acquire Control of an Existing Cemetery Company" or "Transfer of Preneed License" appears under CARRIAGE FLORIDA HOLDINGS INC, buy CSV (~$700M cap, far more acquisition-sensitive per dollar) into its next two prints, since Carriage's whole equity story is deal cadence.
- **Mechanism:** SCI's cemetery segment — not funerals — is where its earnings surprises come from, and SCI's own 10-Q names the driver: Q2 2026 comparable cemetery revenue +4.8% was attributed to preneed sales production growth of $29.7M / +8.0%, with the filing stating "Gross profit was impacted by higher selling compensation, reflecting strong preneed sales production growth." Preneed cemetery property revenue is recognized once the property is constructed and available for interment and the receivable is collectible — so on developed inventory, production converts to recognized revenue fast, and the remainder builds the deferred backlog SCI touts. Preneed cemetery contracts are not order-takers' business; they are sold door-to-door and at-need-adjacent by commissioned counselors. Production is therefore roughly (counselor headcount) x (productivity), and headcount is the variable management actually controls quarter to quarter. A new counselor must be licensed BEFORE selling, and ramps over roughly two to three quarters. So licensure volume is a hard, legally-mandated, forward-looking capacity meter: a hiring surge in month M mechanically caps and floors production in quarters M+1 through M+4. Florida is SCI's densest cemetery-park market (retiree in-migration, large memorial parks), so it is a high-beta read on the national number. Falling adds work the same way in reverse and lead margin relief plus revenue deceleration.
- **Who's on the other side:** Sell-side deathcare coverage is skeletal — roughly five to seven analysts on SCI, three or four on CSV — and their models run off CDC death counts, cremation-mix trends, pricing, and buyback math. None of them model salesforce capacity, because SCI stopped disclosing counselor headcount as a metric; the word "counselor" does not appear anywhere in the current 10-Q. The float is dominated by passive index money and dividend/value funds that own SCI as a demographic annuity and re-underwrite it once a year. On the other side of the acquisition leg are holders who learn about a deal only when it lands in the "Business acquisitions, net of cash acquired" line of a 10-Q. They are slow for a structural reason: deathcare is an alt-data desert. There is no card panel (funerals are paid by check, insurance assignment, or trust draw), no app, no meaningful web traffic, no foot-traffic signal worth reading. So the sector never got covered by the vendors, and nobody built the muscle to look for ground truth.
- **Information lead:** Two distinct leads. (1) Hiring: the Addendum A columns show licenses issued weeks before the packet — the July 2026 packet carries original-issue dates from early May through early June — and the agenda is posted at least seven days before the meeting. So you observe a hire roughly two to six weeks after it happens. SCI first reports the resulting production in the quarterly release ~30 days after quarter end, meaning the first partial read is 3-5 months out and the fully-ramped cohort's effect is 6-12 months out. Net usable lead on a capacity inflection: about one to two full quarters. (2) M&A: board approval of an "Application to Acquire Control" is a closing condition, and it is on a public agenda seven-plus days before the vote. The transaction then appears in a 10-Q acquisition note two to five months later, and Florida cemetery deals are essentially never press-released. That leg is a clean two-to-five-month lead on a named, confirmed transaction.
- **Why still under-exploited:** Nothing about this is packaged. It is a ZIP archive of loosely-formatted PDFs attached to a monthly state regulatory board's meeting agenda, hosted on a Florida insurance-regulator CMS with unstable URL suffixes (?Status=Master, ?sfvrsn=...). It is not in Bloomberg, not in Nasdaq Data Link, not sold by YipitData, M Science, Kpler, or anyone else — no vendor sells state funeral-board licensing microdata from any state, let alone normalized across states. Extracting it requires three non-obvious steps stacked together: knowing that Florida uniquely publishes the employer field ("Appointing Entity Name") rather than just the licensee name; knowing the subsidiary mapping (that NEPTUNE MANAGEMENT CORP is SCI, that FPG FLORIDA LLC is Foundation Partners, that NORTHSTAR CEMETERY SERVICES OF FLORIDA is a private consolidator, not a public comp); and knowing that preneed cemetery sales production — a metric that sounds like accounting trivia — is the actual swing factor in SCI's P&L. Public-health and actuarial researchers mine death registrations; nobody mines the licensing of the people who sell graves. The archive going back to 2007 also means the edge was available and unexploited across two full cycles.
- **Rough +EV:** Honest and modest, with a lumpy tail. The primary hiring signal clears ±1.5σ perhaps three to five times a year. Florida is maybe 15-20% of SCI's cemetery production, and headcount plausibly explains 40-60% of production variance (the rest is pricing, large-sale timing, trust income, and consumer confidence), so call it a 60-65% hit rate on the direction of the cemetery production line versus a 50% baseline. SCI moves 4-8% on earnings days and carries cheap implied vol (~22-25%) for a name with this much idiosyncratic operating leverage, which is what makes the options leg worth doing: on 90-150 day calls, expect roughly +80-150% on the ~35-40% of firings that land and -100% on the rest, netting maybe +15-25% expected return per trade with very wide error bars. On a cash-equity expression sized at 5% of book and held two prints, expect 1.5-3% excess return per firing, or roughly 3-6% annualized alpha on deployed capital. The CSV acquisition leg fires less often — one to three times a year — but pays better per event on a $700M-cap serial acquirer whose multiple is a direct function of perceived deal cadence. The whole program costs one person a weekend to build and a cron job to maintain, so the return on effort is far better than the return on capital.
- **Confidence:** Medium. The data source, its cadence, its employer attribution, its 19-year archive, and the P&L mechanism are all verified directly from primary documents, so there is no existence risk — only signal risk. The biggest uncertainty is whether Florida gross adds are true net hiring or partly an administrative artifact: the state processes licenses in batches, and the June 2026 spike to 42 could be a relicensure or reappointment sweep rather than real headcount growth. That is testable and must be tested before sizing — use the PSA Original Issue Date versus PSA Appointment Date columns to strip out transfers, difference the "Active Sales Agents" level from the Administrative Report to get true net of terminations, and regress the resulting Florida net-add series against SCI's reported comparable cemetery preneed sales production growth across the 2007-2026 archive. Secondary risk: SCI manages a national salesforce and could be reallocating counselors into Florida from other states, which would make the signal a geographic-mix read rather than a capacity read — mitigated by building the parallel Texas and California series so you can see the reallocation instead of mistaking it for growth.

## 73. The Guarantor Sweep

**Arena:** financial-market
**Domain:** Pet economy. RULES: institutions only; sanctioned collection

- **Data source:** State feed control officials' commercial-feed / pet-food PRODUCT REGISTRATION tapes — the per-SKU, per-state filing every pet food "label guarantor" must make before selling in that state. Fields include guarantor/registrant name, brand, brand line, individual product name, manufacturer/co-packer ID, issue date, original effective date, registration year, and the filed label itself (guaranteed analysis, ingredient panel, AAFCO nutritional adequacy statement). Companion datasets: state active-feed-licensee and active-feed-FACILITY rosters (which expose contract manufacturers), and state tonnage-report programs. There is deliberately no national registry — AAFCO coordinates standards but aggregates no product database. The fragmentation across ~50 independent agencies is the entire barrier.
- **How to collect it:** All verified live during this research. (1) INDIANA / OISC, running the "USAPlants" platform: https://inplants.oisc.purdue.edu/USAPlantsIN/ProductRegFSA/BrandSearch.aspx — returns HTTP 200, 48KB ASP.NET WebForms page. Set program dropdown ddProgram="2" (Feed Manufacturer). Searchable by txtCompanyName, txtBrandName, txtBrandLineName, txtManufacturerID, ddYear (2024-2027), and crucially by ISSUE DATE and ORIGINAL EFFECTIVE DATE range pickers (wucIssueDateStartDate/EndDate) — that converts it into a date-stamped new-registration tape rather than a static list. Result grid: Company Name | Program Type | EPA ID | Brand Name. Requires Playwright/headless Chrome: I tested three plain-HTTP postback variants (submit-name, __EVENTTARGET, cookie-jar session) and all return the header row only, because the grid renders via a JS modal postback. (2) TEXAS / Office of the Texas State Chemist, fully open, no login, plain HTML tables: https://otsc.tamu.edu/Reports/ActiveFeedLicensee.aspx (verified 2,511 rows: Permit No. | Company Name | Address) and https://otsc.tamu.edu/Reports/ActiveFeedFacility.aspx (verified 2,915 rows, includes out-of-state co-packing plants). (3) PENNSYLVANIA / PAPlants: https://www.paplants.pa.gov/ — same software lineage; Indiana's form still carries a legacy field literally named txtPaPlantsID. (4) KENTUCKY / UK Division of Regulatory Services: rs.uky.edu/regulatory/feed/registration.php and /tonnage.php. (5) Enumerate the remaining ~45 states from AAFCO's directory https://www.aafco.org/state-information/ plus their state-by-state registration-requirement chart; where no web search exists, the registered-product list is a public record — request a CSV by email, usually free or nominal fee. Build: monthly full crawl + diff. ~2-4 months of one engineer; the genuinely hard part is entity resolution on guarantor names across subsidiary shells and inconsistent spellings.
- **The bet / trade:** Primary (event leg): SHORT Freshpet (FRPT) via 3-6 month puts when the tape shows a Tier-1 CPG guarantor (Nestlé Purina, Mars Petcare, General Mills/Blue Buffalo, Post, Colgate/Hill's) executing a >=25-state sweep of refrigerated or fresh-format SKUs. Hold through the second earnings print after those registrations go effective. Secondary (systematic leg): quarterly-rebalanced long/short across FRPT, CHWY, GIS, CENT, BARK, sized on net registered-SKU delta by guarantor (new registrations minus lapsed renewals), put on ~45 days before each print and taken off after. Long CHWY specifically when Chewy-guarantor private-label food SKU registrations accelerate, since private brand is the stated gross-margin lever and CHWY trades violently on margin bps. Horizon: 3-6 months, one to two earnings cycles.
- **Mechanism:** 1) Legal gate: a pet food SKU cannot lawfully ship into a state until its label guarantor registers that specific product with that state's feed control official — per-product fee paid, label submitted and approved. Registration necessarily PRECEDES first shipment. 2) Therefore a national retail launch requires a 40-50 state registration sweep, executed 1-4 months ahead of the retailer shelf reset (US pet resets cluster Feb-Mar and Aug-Sep). The sweep is the earliest legally-required, publicly-visible footprint of a launch that does not yet exist commercially. 3) Fee-backed revealed preference: each SKU costs real money per state per year to keep alive. Paying to renew means the guarantor expects to sell it; letting it lapse means the discontinuation decision is already made internally. Year-over-year registered-SKU delta per brand is thus forward shelf assortment, which maps directly to volume. 4) The manufacturer/co-packer field, joined to the Texas active-facility roster, reveals which contract manufacturer makes which brand — normally an undisclosed trade secret that signals capacity constraints and which co-packer is about to gain or lose a large customer. 5) For FRPT specifically: the entire bull case and multiple rest on a ~95% share moat in refrigerated pet food. A credible Tier-1 entrant compresses that multiple violently, and FRPT has repeatedly moved double digits on competitive-entry headlines. That entry is invisible in every other dataset until launch day, but must appear in the registration tape months earlier.
- **Who's on the other side:** The scanner and panel complex — Circana/NIQ syndicated scanner data, and e-commerce scrapers like YipitData, M Science, Similarweb — which is structurally blind here by construction: a product with zero units sold generates zero scanner records, and a product detail page goes live days-to-weeks before ship, not months. They physically cannot observe a pre-launch SKU. Sell-side channel checks fail too, because retail buyers are under NDA on unlaunched items and will not confirm. Management and IR treat these filings as a routine compliance chore, not disclosure — nobody inside the company models them as a leak, so there is no effort to obscure them. The registrants are not hiding anything; they are complying. The slowness is purely structural: ~50 independent state systems, no national registry, many on ASP.NET WebForms with session state and JS-postback grids and no API (verified: plain HTTP returns headers only), several PDF-only or records-request-only, with wildly inconsistent guarantor-name spellings and subsidiary shells. It is an unglamorous multi-month engineering and entity-resolution slog with no vendor packaging it.
- **Information lead:** New product / category entry: registration precedes first shipment as a matter of law, and in practice sweeps land 1-4 months before the shelf reset. Scanner data only sees it after units actually sell. Net lead ~2-5 months over scanner and e-commerce panels, and ~4-6 months over company disclosure on an earnings call. Discontinuation: fixed renewal deadlines (many states Dec 31 or Jun 30) make the lapse visible ~3-9 months before the shelf decline shows up in scanner data. Co-packer relationships: effectively never disclosed publicly, so the lead is unbounded. Texas licensee and facility roster diffs surface a new entrant's US manufacturing footprint before any press release.
- **Why still under-exploited:** No alt-data vendor sells pet food state registration data. The closest known analogue, Kelly Solutions, covers PESTICIDE registrations for agriculture — pet food is the neglected corner of the same regulatory plumbing, and nobody has walked across. There is deliberately no national registry (AAFCO sets standards and directs you to individual states), so the aggregation work has to be done from scratch across ~50 agencies. Regulatory-compliance consultancies do exist, but they help companies FILE registrations rather than sell the resulting tape as a signal, and client confidentiality cuts directly against them productizing it. Meanwhile the pet-economy investor community anchors hard on Circana/NIQ scanner data and Chewy/Amazon scrapes — all of which are post-shelf by construction. The data is free, public, and sanctioned; the moat is purely that it is tedious, JS-gated, and demands entity resolution nobody wants to do.
- **Rough +EV:** Systematic leg: computable 4x/year across ~5-6 tickers, so ~20-25 positions annually. Assortment delta plausibly explains a modest slice of the volume surprise — estimate ~1.5-3% expected edge per quarterly position (FRPT prints move ±10-20%, so even a small hit-rate tilt monetizes), call it ~6-12% annualized gross on the systematic sleeve before costs. Event leg carries the skew: a genuine category-entry sweep caught 2-4 months ahead of an FRPT competitive shock is worth 15-25%+ on puts, but fires perhaps once every 1-2 years across the complex — lumpy and high-payoff. Costs are trivial: ~2-4 months of one engineer up front, near-zero data cost (public records, a few hundred dollars in state fees for the PDF/records-request states), then ~$1-2k/year to run. Blended, an attractive Sharpe on a small, capacity-constrained book of roughly $10-50M — FRPT/CHWY liquidity and the narrowness of the tradeable pet complex cap it well short of a scalable strategy.
- **Confidence:** Medium. Biggest uncertainty: registration BEHAVIOR may be noisier than the legal theory implies, in two specific ways. (a) Large CPGs may blanket-register defensively — filing SKUs that never launch, or registering just-in-time right at shipment — which would simultaneously collapse the lead and inflate false positives on the "sweep = imminent launch" trigger. (b) History depth: Indiana's year dropdown exposes only 2024-2027, so online back-history is thin, meaning you likely cannot backtest the base rate without state records requests for archived registration files. Without 5+ years of history you cannot calibrate how often a sweep actually converts into a launch, and that calibration is the whole trade. Secondary risk: guarantor entity resolution — brands registered under obscure subsidiary shells or third-party regulatory agents could hide precisely the Tier-1 entrant you most want to catch.
