## 74. The Plaintext Tail

**Arena:** financial-market
**Domain:** OWN-SENSOR RF/BROADCAST CAPTURE of waste or exhaust signals (the Ad Council Minute archetype). RULES: your own receiver, free-to-air or unencrypted only; never decrypt, never intrude

- **Data source:** The ARINC-618 aircraft-registration field and message bodies of unencrypted aircraft datalink traffic — VHF ACARS ("POA"), VDL Mode 2 (including FANS-1/A CPDLC logons), HFDL, and Inmarsat Classic-Aero / Iridium satcom ACARS — broadcast by business jets that are simultaneously INVISIBLE or ANONYMOUS on every commercial flight-tracking feed. Since 2024-25 the FAA's Privacy ICAO Address (PIA) program gives an aircraft a rotating ICAO 24-bit hex not tied to any registry entry, and FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 §803 (implemented via CARES in 2025) lets owners hide their name/address from the public registry. Neither program touches ACARS: ARINC 618 puts the real 7-character tail (e.g. ".N123AB") in the clear in the message header, and ~99% of ACARS is plaintext. Oxford security research ("Undermining Privacy in ACARS," Smailes/Strohmeier/Martinovic) measured that ACARS usage compromises the privacy of ~90.5% of blocked aircraft. So the airplane that is a nameless hex on ADS-B is still shouting its N-number, its OOOI events, its uplinked flight plan, and often lat/lon, over open radio.
- **How to collect it:** Own receivers, all passive, all unencrypted, zero decryption: (1) VHF ACARS on 131.550 / 130.025 / 130.425 / 129.125 / 136.700-136.975 MHz with RTL-SDR or Airspy + `acarsdec` (multi-channel per dongle). (2) VDL Mode 2 on 136.975 CSC + 136.725/.775/.875 with `dumpvdl2` — this also yields FANS-1/A CPDLC logons carrying the registration. (3) Inmarsat Classic-Aero satcom ACARS at ~1545 MHz with a $30 L-band patch + LNA + RTL-SDR + `JAERO` — one such node covers an entire ocean-region footprint. (4) Iridium ACARS via `gr-iridium`/`iridium-toolkit`. (5) HFDL via Airspy HF+ or KiwiSDR + `dumphfdl`. Stack it all with `sdr-enthusiasts/docker-acarshub` (explicitly supports ACARS, VDLM2, HFDL, Inmarsat L-band, Iridium); cross-check and backfill against the free public aggregator app.airframes.io (github.com/airframesio). (6) Run `readsb`/`dump1090` on the same masts to capture raw ADS-B including PIA hexes, then time/space-correlate an ACARS message to a simultaneous PIA track to permanently bind hex ↔ real tail until the PIA rotates. (7) Identity Rosetta stone: archived daily snapshots of the FAA Releasable Aircraft Database (registry.faa.gov/database/ReleasableAircraft.zip), which the FAA itself does NOT archive but which third parties git-scrape with full commit history (github.com/simonw/scrape-faa-releasable-aircraft, MASTER-1..MASTER-9) — pre-§803 commits still contain owner names; fill post-§803 gaps with state aircraft personal-property tax rolls and UCC-1 lien filings. Deployment: 8-12 Raspberry-Pi + dongle + discone nodes (~$150 each) sited near business-aviation fields — KTEB, KHPN, KMMU, KVNY, KPBI, KOPF, KADS/KDAL, KXNA, KOMA, KSDL, KASE, KBED — plus one L-band satcom node. Total build ~$3-6k plus a few hundred a month.
- **The bet / trade:** Long the equity of the screened US small/mid-cap target (roughly $300M-$8B cap), hedged with a sector-ETF short, sized 2-4% per name, plus a small (5-10% of position risk) overlay of 60-90 day 10-20% OTM calls for convexity. Trigger: a de-anonymized tail matched to a known strategic acquirer's flight department or a top-50 PE sponsor makes a non-routine landing at the airport serving a public company's HQ or main plant — conviction escalates sharply when two or more unrelated acquirer tails hit the same field inside 10 business days, or when the same acquirer tail repeats within 3 weeks. Horizon: hold 60-90 days, exit on deal announcement or at expiry. Mirror trade: fade (short, or sell calls into) rumor-driven takeout pops in names where no acquirer aircraft has ever appeared at the relevant field — the absence signal is as tradable as the presence signal and there is no competing dataset that can produce it.
- **Mechanism:** Negotiated M&A still requires physical presence: management presentations, plant and site visits, and confirmatory diligence happen at the target, and principals and deal teams fly private. Those visits cluster 2-8 weeks before signing, with a dense final sprint 5-15 business days out. This was observable on ADS-B for a decade — until the identity link was cut. PIA replaces the ICAO hex with a rotating anonymous address, §803 hides the owner name, and every commercial tracker (FlightAware, Flightradar24, JetNet, ARGUS TRAQPak) participates in LADD/PIA and is contractually obliged to suppress blocked aircraft. But ACARS is a completely separate radio channel governed by none of those programs, and its designers put the tail number in plaintext in the header because that is how the airline's ground system routes the message. So the causal chain is: acquirer decides to bid → deal team books the jet → the jet's ACARS/VDL2 avionics announce its real registration on departure and arrival → your receiver hears it and your archived registry maps that N-number to Blackstone / Thoma Bravo / a Fortune 500 flight department → you geolocate the arrival field against the target's HQ → you position ahead of the 8-K.
- **Who's on the other side:** Options market makers pricing target implied vol off historical vol and public news flow, plus index and passive holders who will sell into the takeout at yesterday's price. More specifically: the entire event-driven jet-tracking cohort that existed until 2024 — funds buying aviation feeds from FlightAware/FR24/JetNet, and the public jet-tracker accounts — all of which went blind in 2024-25 and concluded the channel was closed. They are slow and wrong for structural reasons, not temporary ones: (a) the commercial vendors are participants in LADD/PIA and legally cannot surface blocked aircraft, so no alt-data shop can package this even if it wanted to; (b) reconstructing it requires RF hardware, four different niche decoders, and archived pre-§803 registry commits, not an API key; (c) the underlying research lives in academic security venues (Oxford, Black Hat), which finance does not read. Perversely, the edge WIDENS as more owners enroll in privacy programs — every new PIA enrollment removes another airframe from everyone else's dataset while leaving it fully visible in yours.
- **Information lead:** Two leads stack. (1) Identity lead: effectively permanent versus every commercial feed — they will never show a PIA/§803-blocked owner, so you are not early, you are the only one who sees it at all. (2) Event lead: median 2-8 weeks from the first diligence/site-visit cluster to announcement, with the final management-presentation sprint typically 5-15 business days ahead of the 8-K; Schedule 13D/merger filings are the market's first look. (3) Micro-lead as a bonus: ACARS pre-departure flight-plan and performance-init uplinks name the destination 20-60 minutes BEFORE wheels-up, and satcom/HFDL cover oceanic and off-network legs where ADS-B coverage is blank entirely — so you know where a jet is going before it moves, and you can follow it where ADS-B cannot.
- **Why still under-exploited:** The vacuum was created in 2024-2026 by the privacy regime itself: the crowd that mined this was evicted, and the mainstream consensus is now "you can't track private jets anymore." The replacement channel sits in an odd intersection — RF hobbyists (airframes.io, ACARS Hub, r/RTLSDR) collect ACARS enthusiastically but have zero interest in equities; aviation-security academics documented the exact privacy failure but published it as a privacy critique, not a trading signal; and the alt-data industry is structurally barred from selling it because those same vendors are LADD/PIA participants. Nothing on the Kpler/Vortexa/YipitData/M Science/Ortex shelf does or can do this. The assembly step — pairing time-correlated ACARS registrations with raw PIA ADS-B hexes and then with git-scraped pre-§803 registry commits — is manual, ugly, perishable (PIA addresses rotate), and requires physical receivers at a dozen sites. That combination of unglamorous work and legal-structural moat is exactly why it stays open.
- **Rough +EV:** Firing rate: after filtering home-base ops, recurring board meetings, and known customer/plant routes, expect 30-70 qualified alerts per year from a 10-node network. Hit rate: honestly 8-18% of alerts precede an announced deal within 90 days, versus a ~0.5-1% unconditional 90-day base rate for a given small-cap — a 10-20x lift on a real prior, which is where the edge lives. Payoff: median announced premium ~30%. Structured as hedged long equity, expected value per alert is roughly +3 to +5% over 60-90 days versus the hedge; across 40-60 positions with capital recycled 4x/yr that is plausibly +10 to +20% gross annualized on deployed capital, before costs and heavily fat-tailed — two to six genuine deal hits a year carry the entire book. The small OTM call overlay converts each hit into a 5-10x on that sleeve and is what makes the tail worth paying for; pure naked-call expression is NOT +EV at a 12% hit rate (needs ~17%+ to clear a 6x spread), which is why the core must be hedged stock. Build cost ~$3-6k hardware, ~$300/mo hosting, and roughly one FTE-month to write the correlation and screening pipeline.
- **Confidence:** Medium. Biggest uncertainty by far: ACARS equipage on the specific airframes that matter. Large-cabin jets (G550/G650, Global 6000/7500, Falcon 7X/8X) carrying deal teams are usually FANS-1/A + CPDLC + satcom equipped via Honeywell HD-710 / Collins DL-150 and are loud on ACARS — but mid-size and light jets (Citation Latitude, Phenom 300, Praetor) frequently have no classic ACARS at all, and some newer installs use IP-based datalink (SwiftBroadband IPDLC, Iridium Certus) that is not Classic-Aero decodable. If the acquirer flies a PIA'd mid-size jet with datalink off, you see nothing, and you will never know what you missed. Secondary uncertainties: signal-to-noise is genuinely bad — jets land at HQ-adjacent fields constantly for non-deal reasons, and "airport nearest HQ" is coarse in dense metros (KTEB serves all of Manhattan), so the screen needs heavy behavioral filtering and will still be mostly false positives; and PIA rotation means the hex↔tail map decays and must be continuously re-derived. Finally, a real-world caveat worth counsel: reception here is passive and of unencrypted signals with no decryption and no intrusion, and the resulting inference is observational rather than MNPI (same posture as satellite parking-lot counts), but 47 U.S.C. §605 and ECPA govern the DIVULGENCE and use of intercepted radio communications, and non-US jurisdictions are far stricter — this is a get-an-opinion-first idea, not a plug-it-in idea.

## 75. The Gob Metronome

**Arena:** financial-market
**Domain:** ACOUSTIC AND VIBRATION SENSING of industrial or venue activity. RULES: own sensors in public/lawful locations; institutions only

- **Data source:** Roof-caving microseismicity behind advancing longwall coal faces — the discrete "periodic weighting" pulses generated when the main roof bridges and then collapses into the gob behind the hydraulic shields. Each pulse is an elastic wave escaping a 500-600 m deep asset that is otherwise completely invisible from outside the fence. The event rate, the cumulative seismic moment, the temporal periodicity of the weighting pulses, and the migration of hypocenters along the panel are a direct, continuous, externally-readable production meter for individual longwalls. Target district: the Brookwood / Blue Creek longwall cluster in Tuscaloosa and Jefferson Counties, Alabama (Warrior Met Coal — Mine No. 4, Mine No. 7's two longwalls, and the new Blue Creek longwall), all four faces inside a ~25 km circle. Secondary district: Greene County, PA (Core Natural Resources' Bailey / Enlow Fork / Harvey complex).
- **How to collect it:** Own array, ~5-6 nodes: Raspberry Shake RS4D (~$1,000 ea, raspberryshake.org) or better 3C 5 Hz nodes (SmartSolo IGU-16HR-3C, ~$2-3k ea), buried 0.5 m, solar + LTE backhaul, ringing 33.2-33.5N / -87.1 to -87.5W. No mine property needed — caving events at ~600 m depth are recoverable at 5-15 km. Lawful siting: leased rural parcels with landowner consent, volunteer fire department / church lots, county road ROW under permit. Processing: continuous miniSEED -> STA/LTA plus template matching (EQcorrscan) on the highly repetitive gob-caving waveforms -> local catalog with ML magnitudes -> daily event count, daily summed seismic moment, weighting-interval periodogram, and per-panel hypocenter centroid migration. FREE SUPPLEMENTS I VERIFIED LIVE: (1) Raspberry Shake FDSN, https://data.raspberryshake.org/fdsnws/station/1/query and /fdsnws/dataselect/1/query — a ~10-station citizen cluster (R02E5, R580C, R59E1, R9C99, R9682, RDDCB, RDFFF, RFCEE, R0D8E, R4A3E) was deployed 15-18 Apr 2025 directly over the Greene County PA longwalls and streams free, near-real-time (T-30min, 24h per request). Alabama has ZERO Raspberry Shake coverage within 60 km of Brookwood — pure greenfield. (2) USGS ComCat, https://earthquake.usgs.gov/fdsnws/event/1/query?eventtype=mine%20collapse — returns the Brookwood events (se60505233 M2.21 on 2026-03-20, se60081823 M2.48, us10005hq7, us10005cep M3.0) proving the source mechanism and giving free Gutenberg-Richter anchors. (3) MSHA Mine Data Retrieval System quarterly production per mine ID (msha.gov/data-and-reports/mine-data-retrieval-system, flat files weekly) as free supervised training labels. (4) State permit / mine maps for panel geometry and orientation.
- **The bet / trade:** Primary: directional equity/options position in Warrior Met Coal (HCC, NYSE, liquid options), sized off a quarter-to-date seismic tonnage nowcast, held 2-10 weeks into the quarterly volume release (roughly early May / early Aug / late Oct / mid Feb). Trade it as a pair — long HCC vs. short Alpha Metallurgical (AMR) or a coking-coal swap — to strip out the met coal price beta and isolate the volume surprise, since price is the noisy, already-arbitraged half. Fire only when the nowcast diverges more than ~5% from consensus volume. Secondary and higher-conviction: an event trade on face silence — if the Blue Creek or Mine 7 array goes quiet for more than 5 consecutive production days outside a pre-announced longwall-move window, short HCC / buy 1-2 month puts, hold 1-4 weeks. Same structure on CNR (Core Natural Resources) using the free Greene County PA cluster.
- **Mechanism:** A longwall shearer cuts a ~300 m wide face, advancing roughly 1 m per pass, 15-25 passes/day. Behind the shields the ~600 m overburden must cave. It does not cave smoothly: the main roof bridges across the gob, accumulates strain, and fails in discrete periodic-weighting events every ~10-30 m of face advance. Tons extracted = face width x web depth x seam height x density x passes, so face advance rate IS tonnage, and the caving that advance forces is the thing that radiates. Four consequences: (a) the time interval between weighting pulses is inversely proportional to advance rate, giving a rate estimate that needs no magnitude calibration at all — a literal metronome; (b) summed seismic moment per day scales with the volume of overburden caved, i.e. with tons; (c) silence means the face is not advancing — a longwall move (2-6 weeks of zero production, the single largest swing factor in quarterly met coal volumes), a roof fall, a sealed panel, or a combustion event; (d) when the hypocenter centroid jumps to a new parallel line matching the permit-map panel layout, the longwall move has finished and production has restarted. USGS confirms longwall roof collapses are real, locatable seismic sources and are catalogued as "mine collapse." Warrior's Q3 2024 longwall move slipping into Q4 2024 is exactly the kind of event this reads in real time.
- **Who's on the other side:** Sell-side met coal analysts and fundamental resource funds modelling quarterly volumes off company guidance plus MSHA quarterly data. Also the satellite/alt-data complex (Orbital Insight, RS Metrics and similar) and the coal price reporting agencies. They are slow for a structural reason that does not go away: the productive asset is 600 m underground. Imagery sees a raw coal silo and a prep plant, which lag the face by days and tell you nothing about whether the shearer is cutting; there is no parking lot to count, no stockpile that resolves a longwall move, no thermal plume. MSHA production data is self-reported, aggregated at mine-ID level (so it cannot separate Mine 7's two longwalls), and lands a full quarter late. And the public seismic catalog is actively misleading: I pulled the entire national ComCat "mine collapse" record and it contains 3 events since January 2024, so anyone who checks the free data concludes there is no signal and stops. The real signal is 2-3 magnitude units below the regional detection threshold, and the only way to reach it is to physically bury sensors in rural Alabama — a fieldwork and logistics moat that pure data-purchasing shops will not cross. Notably, mine operators themselves run in-mine microseismic arrays (ESG Solutions, IMS) for burst safety, so the physics is commercially proven; nobody has simply pointed it at the outside of the fence.
- **Information lead:** Unplanned halt (roof fall, ignition, panel sealing): hours, versus an 8-K up to 4 business days later or, more often, the quarterly call — a lead of 1 day to 3 months. Longwall move start and end dates including overrun: same-day, versus the quarterly call — 3 to 13 weeks. Quarter-to-date cumulative tonnage: continuous, versus the production press release roughly 5 weeks after quarter end — 5 to 14 weeks. Versus MSHA MDRS quarterly production, a full quarter plus. Restart confirmation after a halt is the most valuable single leg: you see the face resume the day it resumes, while the market is still pricing an open-ended outage.
- **Why still under-exploited:** Three barriers stack. First, a false negative in the free data — the public catalog holds essentially zero mining events, so casual screening kills the idea before it starts. Second, capital-markets people do not know the rock mechanics, and rock mechanics people (who know periodic weighting cold, and publish on it constantly for burst-hazard reasons) do not trade equities; the literature exists entirely inside mining safety journals. Third, it requires physical deployment on leased rural land rather than a data license, which is anathema to the buy-side alt-data procurement model — you cannot expense this through a vendor. The result: microseismic monitoring is a mature multi-vendor industry sold to mine operators for safety, and has never been repackaged as an external production nowcast for investors. The verified Greene County citizen deployment is the tell — ten free seismographs went up over the largest longwall complex in North America in April 2025 for someone else's reasons (subsidence or academic), stream publicly, and are being used by nobody for this.
- **Rough +EV:** Setup: ~$10-25k hardware plus modest site rent and 2-3 field trips; ~2 quarters of overlap with MSHA labels to calibrate. HCC is a high-fixed-cost miner, so quarterly volume surprises transmit at roughly 1.2-2x into the stock; consensus volume dispersion runs around 5-8%. A nowcast good to +/-5% on QTD tonnage should produce a usable directional call maybe 4-6 times a year on scheduled prints, worth an expected 3-6% per trade on the isolated-volume pair, plus 1-3 unscheduled halt/restart events a year across the four Alabama faces and the three PA faces, where the payoff is larger (5-15%) because you are trading against a genuine information vacuum. Rough gross: 15-30% annualized on a dedicated sleeve, before costs, with roughly two-thirds of it coming from the binary silence/restart signal rather than the tonnage regression. Capacity is small — call it $20-60mm in HCC/CNR/AMR without material impact — which is part of why nobody built it.
- **Confidence:** Medium. Biggest uncertainty: the tonnage regression may be much weaker than the timing signal. The literature is explicit that seismic energy release correlates poorly with face advance rate because magnitude is governed largely by pre-existing fracture geometry and local geology rather than mining intensity — so the absolute tons-per-day estimate could stay noisy even after calibration. The binary and temporal readings (face advancing vs. not, weighting periodicity, hypocenter jump to a new panel) are far more robust and should be treated as the core alpha, with tonnage as a secondary overlay. Secondary risks: Alabama site noise from the surrounding highwall mines, quarries, and CBM operations could contaminate the catalog until template matching is well trained, and long-term site access on leased parcels is a real operational fragility.

## 76. The Unsold Aisle

**Arena:** financial-market
**Domain:** WASTE/UNSOLD/FILLER INVENTORY as a distress readout (generalizing Ad Council Minute). RULES: institutions only; sanctioned collection

- **Data source:** Live `boothstatus` on public B2B trade-show floorplans — the booth-by-booth sold/available/on-hold/reserved ledger that show organizers publish on the open web 6-14 months before each show, plus booth square footage, exhibitor identity, list price, and the hall inventory itself. Verified live: Map Your Show floorplans expose a MapLibre GL vector-tile layer where every booth polygon carries `objecttype` ("booth"/"room"), `boothstatus` (values enumerated in the floorplan bundle: `available`, `onhold`, `reserved`, `pending`, `cart`, `room`, sold), `booth`, `boothdimensions`/`boothdims`, and `exhid`. Confirmed unauthenticated live instances as of Aug 2026: `https://ofc27.mapyourshow.com/8_0/exhview/index.cfm` (OFC 2027, optical/DCI, config `showavailablebooths: "1"`, halls ["OO","C","L","D","L2","K"]); `https://directory.imts.com/8_0/exhview/index.cfm` (IMTS 2026 machine tools, `showavailablebooths: "1"`, 11 halls); `https://packexpo26.mapyourshow.com/8_0/exhview/index.cfm` (PACK EXPO 2026, availability display switched OFF — itself a tell). Same data exists on ExpoFP (`app.expofp.com`, whose public reservation links leak list price directly: `app.expofp.com/reservebooth/4446492?type=STANDARD&price=5400`), Expocad 3e (`new.expocad.com/expocadweb`), and a2z/Momentive. Informa — the world's largest B2B events organizer — is a Map Your Show client.
- **How to collect it:** All public, unauthenticated, no login. (1) Enumerate the panel: ~60 flagship shows across Map Your Show (`{show}.mapyourshow.com/8_0/exhview/index.cfm` = sales view; `/8_0/floorplan/index.cfm` = attendee view), ExpoFP, Expocad 3e, a2z. (2) Per show, weekly: drive the page headless (Playwright), let MapLibre load, then read `map.querySourceFeatures()` on the booth layer, or intercept the vector-tile requests to `https://maps.mapyourshow.com/{show}/…`. Verified working unauthenticated JSON side-doors on MYS: `/8_0/floorplan/remote-proxy.cfm?action=getExhibitorsInBooth&booth=&hallid=`, `?action=getBoothSpatials&booth=&hallid=`, `?action=getLocation&HallID=` (returns `{"success":true,"data":[…]}` with no session). Full sold census via `/8_0/explore/exhibitor-gallery.cfm` and `/8_0/exhibitor/exhibitor-details.cfm?ExhID=`. (3) Compute: booked net square feet (NSF) from `boothdimensions` or polygon area; unsold NSF = total hall booth-polygon area minus sold+onhold (this still works when the organizer turns `showavailablebooths` to "0", which is why hiding it doesn't help them). (4) Track the *filler* substitutions: non-revenue floor objects appearing where booths were — lounges, "innovation zone", startup pavilion, food court, widened aisles — and hall drops (the `halls: [...]` array in the page config shrinking edition-over-edition; e.g. IMTS runs 11 halls, PACK EXPO 6). (5) Build history from archive.org snapshots of prior editions to get same-weeks-to-show baselines. (6) Entity-resolve exhibitor legal/DBA strings to tickers. Respect robots.txt and rate limits; never touch the exhibitor-login contract portal.
- **The bet / trade:** Two legs off one tape. LEG 1 (sector capex, the higher-beta one): at T-20 weeks before each flagship show, rank that show's public-company exhibitors by YoY change in contracted booth NSF and by drop-out/downgrade status; go long the top decile, short the bottom decile, equal-weight, dollar-neutral, entered T-16 weeks and held through the next two earnings prints (~4-7 month hold). First live instances available right now: OFC 2027 (`ofc27.mapyourshow.com`, show spring 2027) → L/S across the optical-interconnect complex — COHR, LITE, FN, AAOI, CRDO, MRVL, POET; IMTS 2026 (`directory.imts.com`, Sept 2026) → machine-tool capex read (HURC, KMT, and the AMT/USMTO order-cycle proxy); ProMat/MODEX → SYM, ZBRA; RSNA → imaging. LEG 2 (pure-play organizer): aggregate unsold NSF across Informa Markets' top ~50 shows into a nowcast of the "% of full-year exhibitor revenue forward booked" figure Informa itself publishes; go long or short Informa plc (INF.L, LSE) entered 3-4 weeks before the FY results (mid-March) and the H1 results (late July), ~6-week hold, sized off the gap between your nowcast and consensus.
- **Mechanism:** Exhibit floor space is perishable inventory sold on a forward contract 6-14 months out, and it is the single largest discretionary line in most industrial/medtech/semis marketing budgets. A company books next year's booth when it believes it will have product to show and customers to sell; it shrinks or drops the booth when the CFO is cutting, when a product ramp has slipped, or when it has lost the account base. So per-exhibitor booth NSF is a hard, money-committed, forward-looking vote on that company's own 12-month demand outlook — made by insiders, disclosed to nobody, but rendered publicly as a colored polygon on the organizer's sales floorplan. Aggregated across a show, the same tape is the sector's capex/confidence census. Aggregated across an organizer's portfolio it is, almost literally, that organizer's revenue: Informa states that commitments for roughly 90% of Informa Markets' full-year exhibitor revenue sit inside its forward-booked figure, and ~80% of group revenue is committed/visible via subscriptions and forward bookings. The distress cascade is visible in a fixed order: (a) sell-through velocity vs. weeks-to-show decays; (b) organizer flips `showavailablebooths` to "0" to hide the holes; (c) unsold space is converted into non-revenue filler — lounges, innovation zones, startup pavilions, food court expansion, wider aisles; (d) a hall is dropped from the plan entirely. Each stage is a timestamped, machine-readable event.
- **Who's on the other side:** Sell-side analysts modeling Informa/RELX off management's twice-yearly forward-bookings commentary, and industrials/semis analysts modeling capex off order books, PMIs and channel checks. They are slow for structural reasons: the only organized dataset in this space is CEIR's Index (IAEE's research arm, powered by Oxford Economics), which reports NSF *sold* on a quarterly, aggregate, retrospective basis — after the shows have already occurred — and is sold to the events industry, not to investors. The exhibiting companies' own IR will never disclose that they halved their booth. The organizers have an active incentive to obscure it and do (hiding availability, papering unsold blocks with "innovation zones"), which analysts read as programming strategy rather than as inventory failure. And the incumbent alt-data vendors have skipped it because there is no single API to license: the data is smeared across six floorplan vendors and hundreds of one-off show subdomains, requires geometry math to turn polygons into NSF, and requires messy entity resolution to reach a ticker.
- **Information lead:** Very large. Booth contracts are signed 6-14 months pre-show, and each contract lands on the public floorplan within days of signature. Versus the organizer: Informa discloses forward bookings twice a year (March, late July), so you see the same commitments continuously with a 3-9 month lead on the print. Versus CEIR: their quarterly NSF index lands ~2-3 months after quarter end, aggregate-only and post-show — a 9-15 month lead at company granularity. Versus the exhibitor: the booth decision anticipates the revenue it is meant to support by roughly 6-12 months, i.e. two to four earnings prints. And there is a lead nobody else has at all — the weekly *booking velocity curve*. Everyone eventually sees the final exhibitor list; only a weekly scraper sees that a show was 42% sold at T-30 weeks when the prior edition was 61%, four months before the sold-out press release papers it over.
- **Why still under-exploited:** It is fragmented, geometric, and annual — three things that make quant screens skip it. There is no vendor selling it: the one commercial dataset (CEIR/Oxford Economics) is aggregate, lagged, post-show, and aimed at the events industry rather than investors; nothing in the Kpler/Vortexa/YipitData/M Science tier covers exhibit floor inventory. Building it requires hand-enumerating ~60 shows across Map Your Show, ExpoFP, Expocad 3e and a2z, each on its own subdomain with its own hall codes; extracting NSF from MapLibre vector-tile polygons rather than reading a field; resolving "Coherent Corp." / "II-VI" / "Finisar" style exhibitor strings to tickers across editions; and reconstructing prior-edition baselines from archive.org. It also *looks* low-frequency — one show per year — which hides the fact that the sales curve is continuous and the panel of ~60 staggered shows produces a weekly signal. Finally, the natural pure-play consolidators have been going private (Emerald/Questex to Apollo, July 2026; Hyve earlier), which has thinned coverage and analyst attention on exactly the mechanism this reads.
- **Rough +EV:** Leg 1: I'd expect a 3-6% gross spread on the top-vs-bottom-decile L/S over the 4-7 month hold, with a ~55-60% directional hit rate on the individual names — the extremes (a company that drops out of its industry's flagship show entirely, or doubles its island booth) should carry most of the alpha, so run it concentrated on the tails, not the middle. A built-out 60-show panel gives ~40-60 raw signals/year, realistically ~15-25 independent bets after sector correlation, so call it 3-6% net on a modest gross book, i.e. a real but not enormous standalone sleeve. Capacity maybe $50-300m before the small-cap short legs (AAOI, POET, HURC) get crowded. Leg 2 fires twice a year: if the nowcast lands within ~150bp of the reported forward-booking percentage, a 2-4% move on INF.L around the print at ~60% hit rate is a fair guess; INF.L is liquid enough to size, though its listed options are thin, so express it in stock or CFD. Cost side is trivial — one machine, Playwright, a few GB of weekly snapshots; the real cost is ~2-3 months of manual work building the show panel and the entity-resolution map, which is exactly the moat.
- **Confidence:** Medium. The data unambiguously exists, is public, is machine-readable, and carries a genuine multi-month lead — I verified the live endpoints and the `boothstatus` field enumeration directly. The biggest uncertainty is signal-to-noise in the booth decision itself: exhibit space is sticky and political — multi-year contracts, onsite rebooking with priority-point systems, and CMO-level budget decisions that can lag or lead the actual business by quarters. A shrinking booth may mean "demand is rolling over" or merely "new CFO cut events spend 20% across the board," and those look identical on the floorplan. Mitigations: use the *cross-sectional* rank within a single show (which nets out show-wide and macro effects), weight the tails, and require corroboration between the NSF delta and outright drop-out. Second-order risk: organizers can and do degrade the public view (PACK EXPO 2026 already has availability display off), so the collection method must survive on polygon-residual math rather than on the availability flag — and if MYS ever gates the tile server, the sold-side census via the exhibitor gallery still survives but the unsold half of the signal degrades.

## 77. The Abatement Clock

**Arena:** financial-market (US-listed single-asset / few-asset mining equities and their options)
**Domain:** DISCIPLINARY AND SANCTION DOCKETS that pre-announce a physical change (the Silenced Curva archetype). RULES: institutions only; sanctioned collection

- **Data source:** MSHA's weekly enforcement bulk files — specifically the abatement-deadline and withdrawal-order fields inside the Violations dataset, plus the mine-status file. Three layers matter: (1) every open 104(a) citation carries ORIG_TERM_DUE_DT and LATEST_TERM_DUE_DT — a public, dated deadline by which the operator must fix the condition; miss it and MSHA converts it into a 104(b) withdrawal order that legally pulls miners out of the affected area until abated. That is a published forward calendar of conditional shutdowns at named mine IDs. (2) The appearance of CIT_ORD_SAFE = "Order" with SECTION_OF_ACT in {104(b), 104(d)(1), 104(d)(2), 104(g)(1), 107(a), 103(k)} at a mine owned by a concentrated public issuer — a physical work stoppage on a specific section, hoist, fan, belt, or longwall face. (3) TERMINATION_DT on that order — the day the area legally reopened, i.e. outage duration and therefore tons lost, before any company statement. The legal hinge: Dodd-Frank §1503(b) requires an 8-K only for §107(a) imminent-danger orders and §104(e) pattern-of-violations notices. The orders that actually stop production the most often — 104(b) failure-to-abate, 104(d) unwarrantable-failure, and 103(k) post-accident control orders — carry no interim disclosure duty at all. They surface publicly only in Exhibit 95 of the next 10-Q. Congress carved out exactly the production-stopping subset.
- **How to collect it:** Free, sanctioned, no login. Pipe-delimited zips on MSHA's legacy Open Government portal at https://arlweb.msha.gov/OpenGovernmentData/OGIMSHA.asp — the page states plainly: "These files are updated every Friday afternoon." Pull weekly and diff: DataSets/Violations.zip (MINE_ID, CIT_ORD_SAFE, SECTION_OF_ACT, VIOLATION_ISSUE_DT, ORIG_TERM_DUE_DT, LATEST_TERM_DUE_DT, TERMINATION_DT, cited 30 CFR standard, S&S flag, negligence, and free-text "condition or practice" narrative); DataSets/OrdersIssued.zip (107(a) imminent-danger orders, broken out separately); DataSets/Mines.zip (CURRENT_MINE_STATUS with values Active / Intermittent / NonProducing / Temporarily Idled / Abandoned, CURRENT_STATUS_DT, CURRENT_CONTROLLER_NAME, CURRENT_OPERATOR_NAME, PRIMARY_SIC); DataSets/Inspections.zip; DataSets/Accidents.zip; DataSets/MinesProdQuarterly.zip for the tons denominator. Field dictionaries are at DataSets/<Name>_Definition_File.txt on the same host. The one piece of real work is the crosswalk nobody has built: MINE_ID → CURRENT_CONTROLLER_NAME (messy legal-entity strings like operating-subsidiary LLCs, not tickers) → SEC CIK → ticker, seeded from Exhibit 95 of each issuer's 10-K, which lists that issuer's mines by MSHA ID. Build it once (a few hundred mines), maintain it quarterly. For 103(k)/103(j) control orders, which are not penalty-bearing violations and may not land in the bulk Violations file, scrape the per-mine reports in the Mine Data Retrieval System at https://www.msha.gov/data-and-reports/mine-data-retrieval-system, and monitor MSHA's fatality/accident alert pages, which post within days. Then run an NLP classifier over the "condition or practice" narrative to separate equipment-level nuisance orders from asset-critical ones (main hoist, slope belt, main fan, longwall shields, escapeway, seal).
- **The bet / trade:** Short single-name equity or buy 30-75 DTE put spreads on US-listed miners where one MSHA mine ID carries the majority of EBITDA, entered on the Friday-file diff and held through the next production update or quarterly print (4-10 weeks). Core universe: Warrior Met Coal (HCC — Mine 4 / Mine 7 / Blue Creek), Ramaco (METC — Elk Creek), Alpha Metallurgical (AMR), Core Natural Resources (CNR — Bailey / Enlow Fork / Harvey), Alliance Resource (ARLP), Hecla (HL — Lucky Friday is ~a quarter of silver output), Coeur (CDE), Intrepid Potash (IPI), MP Materials (MP — Mountain Pass is the entire company), US Lime (USLM). Two triggers, two directions. Short trigger: an asset-critical withdrawal order appears, or a citation on asset-critical equipment gets its LATEST_TERM_DUE_DT extended two or more times (the operator cannot fix it, so 104(b) is coming). Long trigger, the underrated half: after a publicly known outage, TERMINATION_DT populates in a Friday file — production legally resumed — typically days to weeks before the restart press release; buy calls or cover there. Exit on the earnings print, on TERMINATION_DT, or on a CURRENT_MINE_STATUS flip back to Active.
- **Mechanism:** An MSHA withdrawal order is not a fine, it is a statutory command to remove miners from the affected area until the condition is abated. Miners out means the section, shaft, or face physically stops. These are extreme fixed-cost businesses: tons not produced are revenue lost outright, and the remaining fixed cost spreads over a smaller denominator, so a volume miss arrives with a unit-cost miss attached — a double hit to a levered P&L. At a single-asset issuer there is no portfolio to absorb it: one order on the only hoist is the whole quarter. The magnitude precedent is documented — in January 2012 MSHA ordered Hecla's Lucky Friday closed to clear the main silver shaft after a rock burst; production did not resume until 2013, Hecla laid off ~42% of the mine's workforce, and the equity was repriced violently on the order itself. That was the visible tail. The systematic edge lives in the invisible middle: the 104(b) and 104(d) orders that cost two to six weeks on one section, never make a press release, never trigger an 8-K, and show up only as an unexplained volume miss on the call.
- **Who's on the other side:** Sell-side mining analysts, who model tons from company guidance and, at best, from MSHA's quarterly Part 50 production file that lands ~6 weeks after quarter end. Passive and retail holders of high-beta miners. And the issuer itself, which is on the other side by omission rather than intent: it has no legal duty to disclose a 104(b), 104(d), or 103(k) order intraquarter, so silence is the compliant default and the outage is simply absorbed into the next guidance revision. Meanwhile the actual consumer base of MSHA enforcement data is entirely non-financial — safety consultants, union safety reps, plaintiffs' counsel, and law-firm compliance trackers (Fisher Phillips publishes a public MSHA violations tracker; the only scraper on Apify is marketed for safety analysis). They read the same rows for a completely different purpose and would not know what a put spread was for. Nobody is converting a compliance feed into a tons-lost nowcast.
- **Information lead:** Worst-case staleness is seven days (the Friday afternoon refresh); typical lead is three to five days from order issuance. Against the actual competing information: 4 to 13 weeks ahead of Exhibit 95 of the 10-Q, which is the first and usually only place these orders are ever disclosed; 6 to 14 weeks ahead of MSHA's own quarterly production file, the tool coal analysts do use; and effectively infinite against media, which covers fatalities and nothing else — a three-week longwall stoppage at a met coal mine generates zero coverage. The abatement-deadline layer is better than a lead, it is a forecast: ORIG_TERM_DUE_DT and LATEST_TERM_DUE_DT hand you the date on which a citation is scheduled to convert into a shutdown order, before the shutdown exists, and repeated extensions are a public tell that the operator is losing the repair.
- **Why still under-exploited:** Four independent reasons it has stayed unpicked. First, wrong-industry framing: it is filed and consumed as an occupational-safety compliance dataset, and its whole user community is lawyers and safety officers, so it has never been indexed by the alt-data world. Second, delivery friction: pipe-delimited zips on a decommissioned-looking arlweb.msha.gov host with no API, no ticker field, and a controller-name column full of operating-subsidiary legal entities — the mine-to-CIK crosswalk has to be hand-built from Exhibit 95s and is the actual moat. Third, universe size: maybe 25-40 US-listed issuers qualify, which is far too small a TAM for anyone to build a Kpler-equivalent around, and there is no mine-enforcement vendor in existence. Fourth and most important, the core insight is legal rather than quantitative — you have to notice that Dodd-Frank §1503 mandates an 8-K for 107(a) and 104(e) but pointedly not for 104(b), 104(d), or 103(k), which means the disclosure regime exempts precisely the orders that stop production. That is a footnote in securities law, not a signal any data-mining exercise would surface. Academic work linking MSHA violations to returns exists; no one has productized the abatement calendar.
- **Rough +EV:** Lumpy and event-driven, not a smooth Sharpe. Across the 25-40 name universe I'd estimate 8-20 asset-critical orders per year, of which 4-8 materially bend a quarter. These are high-operating-leverage, high-beta equities where a volume-plus-unit-cost miss routinely produces a 5-15% single-name move. Buying 30-60 day put spreads at roughly 1.5-3% of notional against a 35-45% hit rate on a 6-12% adverse move gives roughly +20% to +60% EV per event on premium deployed; at the portfolio level, call it 3-8% annualized on modest capital with most of it arriving in two or three trades, plus a genuine fat tail (the Lucky Friday closure order was a ~25% one-day repricing). The long/restart leg is smaller in magnitude but has a materially higher hit rate, because TERMINATION_DT is unambiguous — production either legally resumed or it did not — and the restart press release reliably lags it.
- **Confidence:** Medium. Biggest uncertainty by far: bindingness. Most withdrawal orders cover one guard, one belt, or one working section in a multi-section mine and cost hours, not weeks — so the entire edge collapses to how well you can read the free-text "condition or practice" narrative to separate a conveyor guard from the main hoist, the main fan, an escapeway, or the longwall face. Get that classifier wrong and you are trading noise at high option-premium cost. Two secondary risks: MSHA enforcement intensity is politically and budget-cyclical, so raw order counts drift for reasons unrelated to mine conditions and you must normalize within-mine over time rather than cross-sectionally; and 103(k) control orders — the fastest and most production-destructive subset, issued within hours of an accident — are not penalty-bearing violations and may not appear in the bulk Violations file at all, forcing you into per-mine MDRS scraping for the very cases where speed matters most.

## 78. The Porcelain-Stone Ledger

**Arena:** financial-market
**Domain:** ADMINISTRATIVE ORDERS THAT REMOVE CAPACITY on a known future date. RULES: institutions only; sanctioned collection

- **Data source:** Chinese provincial/municipal mining-administration registries, read as a forward calendar of dated capacity kills. Three stacked government sources, all public: (1) 采矿许可证 mining-licence registries ("有效采矿权信息查询") run by each provincial 自然资源厅, which publish licence number, mine name, holder, mineral, production scale and — critically — 有效期限, the exact expiry date, visible 1–5 years ahead; plus the national 全国矿业权人勘查开采信息公示系统 mandated by MNR Order No. 13 (《矿业权人勘查开采信息管理办法》, in force 2024-07-01). (2) Municipal bureau 公告/公示 pages that post revocation notices with statutory countdowns — e.g. the Yichun Natural Resources Bureau notice of 2025-12-12 cancelling 27 mining licences (17 registered as ceramic clay, 7 limestone, 3 kaolin/quartzite) effective after a 30-working-day notice period. (3) Provincial 应急管理厅 non-coal-mine 安全生产许可证 registries and their "关于拟核发非煤矿山《安全生产许可证》单位名单的公示" pre-issuance lists (3-year validity), which gate restarts. Optional fourth gate: provincial 生态环境厅 环评受理/拟审批公示 and land-use (用地/林地) 批复 notices. The legal engine is brand new: the revised Mineral Resources Law effective 2025-07-01 made lithium a standalone mineral, so every Yichun lepidolite mine operating under a "ceramic clay / porcelain stone / kaolin" permit is now legally defective and must re-file reserve-verification reports to change its primary mineral.
- **How to collect it:** Nightly scrape + diff, ~200 lines of Python and a translation call. Seed a watchlist of ~40 mines that matter: the 8 Yichun lepidolite rights (Jianxiawo 枧下窝, Shiziling 狮子岭, Baishuidong 白水洞, Huashan 化山瓷石 etc., ~160kt LCE/yr combined) plus Qinghai/Sichuan/Hunan/Xinjiang lithium, and extend to fluorspar/tungsten/antimony/phosphate. Then: (a) query each provincial 自然资源厅 "有效采矿权信息查询" form (e.g. zrzyt.nx.gov.cn/kydwcx/yxckq/ pattern; Jiangxi at zrzyt.jiangxi.gov.cn) and store the 有效期限 end date per licence — this is your hard-stop calendar; (b) crawl the 公告/公示 sections of the prefectural bureaus (宜春市自然资源局 and peers) keyword-filtered on 锂 / 锂瓷石 / 陶瓷土 / 瓷石 / 注销 / 吊销 / 延续; (c) crawl the provincial 应急管理厅 site (Jiangxi: yjglt.jiangxi.gov.cn) for 非煤矿山安全生产许可证 issuance and pre-issuance 公示 lists; (d) crawl 生态环境厅 环评 acceptance/approval notices; (e) map licence holders to listed parents via 国家企业信用信息公示系统 (gsxt.amr.gov.cn / gsxt.amr.jiangxi.gov.cn). No login, no scraping of private data, no paywall — these are statutory administrative-transparency disclosures. The pain is real and is the moat: 31 provinces × 3 agencies, no API, no RSS, no bulk export, inconsistent JS forms, keyword-only search, Chinese-only.
- **The bet / trade:** Event-driven, two-legged, 2–6 week holds around registry dates. Bullish leg: when a tracked mine's 有效期限 lands inside 60 days and the registry shows no renewal paperwork moving (no reserve-verification filing, no 环评 acceptance, no pre-issuance safety-licence 公示), buy 1–3 month out-of-the-money calls / call spreads on Albemarle (ALB, most liquid optionable Western lithium beta) and buy Pilbara Minerals (PLS.AX) outright, or go long CME Lithium Carbonate CIF CJK futures (LTC) / Lithium Hydroxide CIF CJK (LTH) for a purer, cash-settled expression. Bearish leg — the higher-frequency edge: when the 应急管理厅 posts the pre-issuance or issuance of a 安全生产许可证 for a suspended mine, or the 自然资源厅 shows a renewed 采矿许可证, sell/short the same complex (ALB puts, short PLS.AX, short LTC) into the 5–15 day window before Fastmarkets/S&P/Reuters carry it. If accessible, GFEX lithium carbonate (LC) is the highest-beta venue but foreign access is restricted. Secondary expression: permit-renewal questions posted on Manifold/Polymarket (one already ran: "CATL receives license renewal for Yichun Lithium mine by Feb 1, 2026") resolve directly off this registry data.
- **Mechanism:** A Chinese mine is legally dead the day its 采矿许可证 lapses, regardless of ore body, capex or offtake. Jianxiawo alone is ~100kt LCE/yr nameplate and was 8–10% of China's lithium carbonate output; China is the marginal swing supplier of lithium chemicals. So: licence expiry or revocation → production physically stops → Chinese carbonate spot and GFEX futures repricing → Fastmarkets/SMM assessments follow → Western lithium equities (ALB, PLS, SQM, SGML, LIT) mark to the new price. Verified magnitude: Jianxiawo's licence expired 2025-08-09, CATL confirmed suspension 2025-08-11, and the GFEX September LC contract opened limit-up +8% and closed +11.36% (72,340 → 80,560 yuan/t). The reverse runs on restart: the mine could not resume until it walked back through land-use approval, environmental approval and finally a 安全生产许可证, which it obtained 2026-06-29 — and it resumed operations essentially that week. Each of those gates is a separate, separately-published administrative act with its own public notice, so the restart is a sequence of visible checkpoints, not a surprise announcement.
- **Who's on the other side:** Long-only EV/materials thematic funds and the LIT ETF; Western lithium equity holders in ALB/SQM/PLS who model demand curves and Chilean royalties, not Chinese administrative licensing law; GFEX retail speculators reacting to Cailianshe headlines; and the price-reporting agencies themselves. The PRAs (Fastmarkets, SMM, Benchmark, S&P Commodity Insights) are survey shops — they phone producers and traders and publish when a company confirms or a Chinese wire reports. They do not diff permit registries. Sell-side lithium analysts cannot read a provincial 自然资源厅 query form and would not know that "陶瓷土" (ceramic clay) is how a third of China's lepidolite supply is legally titled. The listed owners are Chinese A-shares (Jiangte 002176.SZ, Yongxing) and an unlisted CATL subsidiary — none has a prompt duty to disclose permit status, so the government registry is legally obliged to be first while the company is free to be last.
- **Information lead:** Three different leads, measured against real events. (1) Restart leg, empirically verified: the Jianxiawo 安全生产许可证 was obtained 2026-06-29; S&P Global's headline "China's lithium markets muted amid CATL securing mine safety permit" ran 2026-07-08 — a 9-day lead, sitting in a public provincial registry the whole time. The pre-issuance 拟核发 公示 list adds several more days on top. (2) Revocation leg: statutory public-notice windows are 20–30 working days before the licence dies (Yichun's 27-licence notice, 2025-12-12, effective ~late January 2026); the marquee names get picked up by Yicai within days but prefectural notices on smaller holders go essentially unreported in English. (3) Expiry leg, the biggest: the 有效期限 end date is in the registry 1–5 years ahead, while the market prices it 0–2 days ahead — Jianxiawo expired 9 August and futures did not move until the 11th. Nobody was reading the date.
- **Why still under-exploited:** No vendor sells Chinese mining-permit registry monitoring. The commercial lithium data stack is price assessments (Fastmarkets, Benchmark, SMM, Argus) and plant-level survey research (Mysteel, SMM) — both downstream of the administrative act, both dependent on someone talking. Satellite/alt-data shops watch mine activity, which tells you a mine stopped, not that it will stop in 47 days. The structural reason it is not productised: the data is split across 31 provinces × 3 agencies (自然资源厅 for mining rights, 应急管理厅 for safety licences, 生态环境厅 for EIA), plus prefectural bureaus, each with a bespoke Chinese-only keyword form, no API, no bulk export, no RSS. And the regime is genuinely new — MNR Order No. 13 on mining-rights disclosure took effect 2024-07-01, and the revised Mineral Resources Law reclassifying lithium as a standalone mineral only took effect 2025-07-01. That law is what converted a decade of quietly mining lepidolite under ceramic-clay permits into a dated, enumerated, publicly-noticed compliance cliff. There is no institutional muscle memory for reading it because it is roughly one year old.
- **Rough +EV:** Roughly 6–15 datable registry events per year in lithium alone (8 Yichun rights forced to reclassify, the 27-licence revocation list, plus Qinghai/Sichuan/Hunan/Xinjiang renewals), more if extended to fluorspar, tungsten, antimony and phosphate. Observed move sizes: +11.4% single-day in GFEX LC and high-single-digit in ALB on the shutdown; the restart print was "muted" because it was partly anticipated — so the asymmetry is real, shutdown surprises are worth roughly 3× restart surprises and the bullish leg should carry most of the risk budget. With a 5–15 day lead expressed in 1–3 month options, realistic capture is +2% to +5% net per event on deployed notional at a ~55–60% hit rate, i.e. plausibly 12–30% annualised on an allocated sleeve, with lumpy returns and long flat stretches. Setup cost is one engineer-week plus a translation API; carrying cost is near zero. Capacity is capped — CME LTC/LTH are thin and GFEX is largely closed to foreigners — so this is a small-team edge, which is exactly why it survives.
- **Confidence:** Medium. Biggest uncertainty is publication latency and completeness at the provincial/prefectural level: some bureaus batch-publish 公示 lists monthly or bury a renewal in a PDF attachment, and if a decisive approval is granted but not posted for two weeks the 9-day lead evaporates on that event. Second-order risk is beta contamination — ALB and PLS also trade on Chilean royalty policy, Nevada assets and EV demand, so the clean expression (GFEX LC) is the one a small foreign team cannot easily reach, and CME LTC/LTH liquidity may not absorb size. Third: the edge decays if a Chinese wire (Cailianshe) or SMM starts systematically diffing the same registries, which is a cheap thing for them to do once someone demonstrates it works.

## 79. The Sixth Rubber

**Arena:** gambling
**Domain:** OFF-RECORD COMPETITIVE ACTIVITY that official databases exclude (the Spielbericht archetype). RULES: institutions/leagues/published results only, never individuals' private behavior; sanctioned collection

- **Data source:** Rubber-level results from European national club/team tennis leagues — real competitive matches played by ATP/WTA/Challenger pros that award zero ranking points and appear in no tennis database. Each tie is 4 singles + 2 doubles rubbers; the two doubles rubbers (the "fifth and sixth") are where hired pros quietly double their same-day match load and are absent from every dataset that exists. Leagues: German 1./2. Tennis-Bundesliga (Jul–Aug, verified 2026 roster incl. Tsitsipas, Darderi ATP 16, Vacherot ATP 20, Rinderknech ATP 28), Swiss Interclub NLA (May–Jun, 28 top-200 players in a recent edition), French Championnat Interclubs Pro A (Nov–early Dec; Gasquet, P-H Herbert, Roger-Vasselin at Villa Primrose), Italian Serie A1 (group phase Oct 5–Nov 9, semis Nov 16–23, final Dec 6–8), Czech Extraliga, Austrian/Belgian/Dutch equivalents. Fields available nowhere else: set-by-set scores, lineup position (the club's own strength ranking), doubles pairings, mid-rubber retirements, attendance, and session start/end times.
- **How to collect it:** Verified live, not theoretical. Germany: GET https://dtb.liga.nu/cgi-bin/WebObjects/nuLigaTENDE.woa/wa/groupPage?championship=BL+2026&group=2133154 returns HTTP 200 (curl with a browser UA; WebFetch gets 503, so set the UA) and contains one /wa/meetingReport?meeting=<id>&federation=DTB&championship=BL+2026 link per fixture. I pulled meeting=12555574 (Kurhaus Lambertz Aachen 2:4 Badwerk Gladbacher HTC, Sun 09.08.2026): full rubber table — "Gaubas, Vilius LTU (6)" l. "Squire, Henri GER (11)" 1:6 6:4 7:10; Passaro (ITA) l. La Serna (ARG); Skatov (KAZ) d. Pucinelli de Almeida (BRA); doubles incl. Jebens/Pütz vs La Serna/Kohlschreiber; "Zuschaueranzahl: 1100"; "Spielbeginn: 9:00 Uhr, Spielende: 17.00 Uhr"; plus a PDF report link. The same nuLiga/WebObjects engine serves every German Landesverband (tvbb.liga.nu, baden.liga.nu, …) and the Austrian federation. Italy: fitp.it national-championship pages plus tennistalker.it/competizione/76951 (Serie A1 Maschile 2025). France: fft.fr / ten'Up interclubs Pro A results. Switzerland: swisstennis.ch/interclub-nla-herrenteams. Backfill/sanity cross-check on singles only: tennisexplorer.com/bundesliga-men/<year>/atp-men/ (2006–present). Build: ~200 lines of Python + requests + lxml, nightly cron Fri–Mon inside each league's window, joined to ATP/WTA entry lists (protennislive.com, atptour.com) and to the official record (Sackmann tennis_atp, tennis-data.co.uk). Hardest part is name resolution: "Boscardin Dias, Pedro BRA*" → ATP player ID.
- **The bet / trade:** Three legs off one feed. (1) Fatigue fade — back the OPPONENT moneyline, or lay on Betfair, of any Challenger/ATP-250/qualifying player who logged >=3 club-league rubbers (singles + doubles across a Sat/Sun tie) within 72h of first serve; also playable as first-set winner or -1.5 games first-set handicap. Horizon: one match, settles same day. (2) Injury early-warning — a mid-rubber retirement/"aufgegeben" or a walkover in a Sunday tie: lay that player in the following week's tour-event outright and next-match markets. Horizon 1–7 days. (3) Offseason form — during the dead window (Nov 15 – Dec 20) use Italian Serie A1 and French Pro A rubber results, the only competitive tennis being played, to price Australian Open outright / "reach QF" specials and Brisbane–Adelaide–Auckland winner markets on Betfair. Horizon 4–8 weeks to settlement.
- **Mechanism:** Club leagues pay appearance money and award no ranking points, so pros slot them into what the tour calendar shows as rest weeks. A hired pro is his club's #1 or #2 and typically plays a singles rubber AND a doubles rubber the same day inside an eight-hour session (verified: 9:00–17:00), then repeats it the next matchday — best-of-3 with a 10-point match tiebreak, on German/Swiss clay or Italian/French indoor hard. That is real match load plus a flight in and out. Every price in the market, however, is generated by an Elo/points model whose features — surface Elo, days-since-last-match, sets played in last 14 days, retirement flags — are computed from a results pipeline that structurally excludes these matches, because they have no tournament ID, no ranking points, and no rights-holder selling the feed. So "days since last match" is simply wrong, by up to two weeks, for a few hundred player-events a year. The effect is symmetric and that is what makes it tradeable in both directions: a player back from layoff who wins two club rubbers cleanly is match-fit while the market is still pricing rust (back him); a top-100 who loses a rubber to a #400 has a level problem Elo cannot see (fade him); a retirement on Sunday is the earliest possible signal of a Monday withdrawal. In Nov–Dec the mechanism inverts into a pure information-vacuum play: AO and January markets are open and priced on October form, and Serie A1 / Pro A are the only competitive matches happening.
- **Who's on the other side:** Tennis prices originate from a handful of market-makers (Pinnacle plus Asian/feed-driven originators) running point-based and Elo models over commercial result feeds — Sportradar, Genius, Enetpulse — none of which carry federation club leagues. There is no tournament ID to key on, so the data cannot enter their pipeline even in principle without a bespoke ingest. Downstream books copy those lines; recreational money follows ATP ranking and recency, both of which say "rested." The tell that nobody models it: I could not find a single bookmaker offering a market on Tennis Bundesliga ties themselves. The syndicates who could build it face six federations, five languages, PHP/WebObjects HTML with no API, no player IDs, and mid-season roster churn — a build cost wildly disproportionate to a few hundred firings a year on Challenger-sized limits. It is a small-TAM data problem: too fiddly for a vendor to package and sell, too low-ceiling for a serious syndicate to prioritise, so it sits unbuilt.
- **Information lead:** Structural more than temporal — the market does not learn this late, it never learns it at all until the player underperforms on court. The nuLiga meetingReport publishes within minutes of a tie finishing (~17:00 CET Sunday), and no downstream model ingests it, ever. Practical windows: 12–48 hours before a Monday/Tuesday Challenger or qualifying first round; 1–3 days on an injury (retirement in a Sunday rubber → ATP withdrawal posted Monday or Tuesday, and there is no injury-reporting regime in tennis at all); 4–8 weeks on January/AO markets priced off December Serie A1 and Pro A rubbers.
- **Why still under-exploited:** No vendor sells team-tennis rubber data. It is absent from tennis-data.co.uk (ATP/WTA tour only, 2000–), Sackmann's tennis_atp (tour/Challenger/ITF), Tennis Abstract, and the Sportradar/Genius/Enetpulse feeds. Being honest about the one real leak: TennisExplorer does carry Bundesliga men's SINGLES back to 2006 (verified at tennisexplorer.com/bundesliga-men/2026/atp-men/, and it even shows odds on a handful of historical rows), so German singles results are not literally invisible to a diligent person. But it omits the two doubles rubbers — which is precisely where the same-day load doubles and where the whole fatigue signal lives — along with lineup position, session start/end times, and retirements, and its coverage of Swiss Interclub, French Pro A, Italian Serie A1 and Czech Extraliga is thin to nonexistent. The exploitable core is therefore the total same-weekend rubber count including doubles, plus the four non-German leagues, and that exists only on the federation platforms in un-joined, un-IDed, multilingual HTML. Nobody has assembled it because assembling it is genuinely tedious and the payoff is a boutique edge rather than a business.
- **Rough +EV:** Firings: Germany alone is ~9 matchdays x 10 clubs x ~4 imported pros ≈ 300–400 pro-weekends across Jul–Aug, plus Switzerland (May–Jun), Italy (Oct–Dec), France Pro A (Nov–Dec), Czech/Austria. After filtering to players with an official match inside 5 days, roughly 150–300 qualifying fatigue bets a year, plus 10–25 offseason futures positions. Edge sizing: an extra 2–3 hours of competitive load in the prior 72 hours is worth roughly 2–4 percentage points of win probability in an evenly matched pair; against Challenger/qualifying overrounds of 5–7% (3–4% at Pinnacle) that nets maybe 3–6% ROI per bet. At Challenger limits of $500–1,500 that is only ~$3k–15k/yr on the fatigue leg. The offseason futures leg carries the real money — AO outrights see $50k–500k matched on Betfair and are priced on six-week-old information, so a Dec 7 Serie A1 final result or a Pro A retirement can shift a fair price 10–20% relative on a 40/1–100/1 runner, at 8–15% ROI on meaningful size. Blended honest guess: 4–8% ROI on 200–300 plays/year, i.e. $20k–60k/yr at achievable limits. Decays to near zero the day any feed vendor adds team tennis.
- **Confidence:** Medium. Data existence and collectability are verified, not assumed — I pulled a live 2026 fixture and got the full rubber table, and confirmed the parallel Italian, French and Swiss leagues by their published calendars and rosters. Market invisibility is high-confidence: no book prices these ties, and the data is in none of the standard tennis datasets. The biggest uncertainty by far is the SIZE of the fatigue coefficient. Pros hired for appearance money have every incentive to coast, tank a dead rubber, or retire early to protect themselves, so raw minutes may badly overstate true physiological load — and the match-sharpness effect could partially or wholly offset it, making the sign ambiguous rather than merely the magnitude. This is settleable before risking money: reconstruct 2015–2025 Bundesliga and Serie A1 participation, join to each player's next official match, and regress. If the coefficient comes back under ~1.5pp, kill the fatigue leg entirely and keep only the injury early-warning and offseason-form legs, which rest on information asymmetry rather than on a physiological effect size.

## 80. The D-Number Panel

**Arena:** gambling — US regulated sportsbooks, NASCAR Cup / O'Reilly Auto Parts (Xfinity) / Truck Series
**Domain:** EQUIPMENT AND SPEC CHANGES that alter performance (the Tungsten Tell archetype). RULES: manufacturer/governing-body published data only; sanctioned collection

- **Data source:** Goodyear's per-race NASCAR tire specification releases — the "Goodyear Racing Notes" issued for every national-series event. Each release publishes the exact left-side and right-side Goodyear Racing Eagle tire CODE (e.g. Richmond 2026: D-6142 left / D-6116 right; Nashville 2026: D-6110 / D-6148; Texas 2026: D-5284 / D-5290), the explicit prior-usage list for that code combination ("previous usage in 2026 at Las Vegas, Darlington and Kansas"), the set allotment, the tire circumferences (stagger), and Goodyear's minimum recommended inflation pressure at each corner. The load-bearing fact, stated in Goodyear's own NASCAR Tire Manual: "When any part of the construction or compound is changed, the D number will be changed." The D-number is therefore a manufacturer-published, atomic spec-change key — a hash of the actual rubber. Paired second feed: the NASCAR/Goodyear tire-test rosters, which name the two or three specific Cup organizations and drivers who get to run an unreleased compound on a given track months before the race (e.g. Chicagoland, April 2026: Blaney, Hamlin, Larson; Iowa, May 2026: Dillon, Gragson, Reddick). No public database joins either feed to results.
- **How to collect it:** All free, public, sanctioned press material. (1) Weekly codes: scrape the syndicated Goodyear release every Tue–Wed of race week from jayski.com ("Goodyear Racing Notes: <track>" posts), speedwaydigest.com (same wire copy), nascar.com/news-media (weekly tire preview article), and Goodyear.com/Racing. Regex `D-\d{4}` for left/right codes plus the prior-usage sentence, the set-allotment integer, and the per-corner minimum pressures. (2) Historical panel: Jayski has archived these same releases weekly for well over a decade — one backfill crawl builds the code-by-track-by-race table nobody else has. (3) Tire-test rosters: the standing page https://www.jayski.com/goodyear-news-and-tire-testing/ plus NASCAR.com tire-test previews. (4) Spec semantics: Goodyear Racing NASCAR Tire Manual PDF (mirrored at hscra.us/PDF/nascar_goodyear_tire_manual.pdf). (5) Join target: race results and loop data via Racing-Reference or the CRAN R package `nascaR.data` (v3.0.1, Cup 1949–present) — which, tellingly, has no tire field at all. Total build: one weekend of scraping plus a nightly cron.
- **The bet / trade:** NASCAR Cup Series driver HEAD-TO-HEAD MATCHUP money lines (two-way, ~-110/-115) at DraftKings / FanDuel / BetMGM / Caesars, entered Tuesday–Thursday of race week and held to the checkered flag Sunday (3–5 day settlement). Direction: BACK the driver whose D-number-matched history (his finishes at other tracks that ran this same code) is strong while his track-label history is weak; FADE the driver the market is pricing on "he's good at this track" when the compound under him this week is not the compound he was good on. Second leg, higher variance: at races where Goodyear brings a code with NO prior usage anywhere, take TOP-10 FINISH and TOP-5 props (+150 to +400) on drivers from the two or three organizations that ran the Goodyear tire test at that track. Run the same book in the O'Reilly Auto Parts and Truck series, where Goodyear publishes identical notes and the matchup lines are softer. Exit rule: stop betting the race once Saturday practice speeds post — that is when the edge is consumed.
- **Mechanism:** Goodyear changes compound or construction → the D-number changes → peak grip, falloff rate, thermal window and stagger change → the optimal setup window and the rewarded driving style change (rotation-on-entry vs. drive-off, tire-conservation vs. raw single-lap pace). Two exploitable consequences follow. First, driver-track "fit" — the core feature in every public NASCAR model — is mis-specified. Models key on the track label (1.5-mile oval, short track, road course), but the physical determinant of who is fast is the rubber, and Goodyear reuses the same code across physically dissimilar venues: D-6110 ran at both Las Vegas asphalt and Nashville concrete in 2026; D-5284/D-5290 ran at Las Vegas, Darlington, Kansas and Texas. So the correct similarity key for driver fit is the D-number, not the track type, and the two disagree several times a season. Second, when a code is brand-new, the only humans with data on it are the two or three teams Goodyear invited to test — and NASCAR's 2026 rulebook bans organizational testing within 60 days of an event, at repaved tracks, and at tracks new to the schedule, making the Goodyear test the only legal track time on that rubber. That monopoly propagates through the whole organization, not just the test driver: Denny Hamlin tested Chicagoland in April 2026; in July, Joe Gibbs Racing finished 1-2-3 there with Briscoe, Bell and Hamlin. Layer on the option-tire era (softer red-lettered compound with deliberate falloff, allotments announced only in these notes) and the 2026 750-hp / short-track aero package now in force at Bristol, Darlington, Dover, Nashville and WWT, and the market's track-history priors are the stalest they have been since 2022.
- **Who's on the other side:** Recreational NASCAR money — the largest share of the handle — betting driver names and "he wins here." Behind it, book traders and the market-making feeds pricing off loop data, recent finishes, and track-type buckets. Every public analytics asset in the sport is tire-blind: Racing-Reference carries no tire column, the CRAN `nascaR.data` package carries no tire column, NASCAR's own loop data carries no tire column, and DFS tools (RotoWire, Action Network, Racing Insights) model by track archetype. The people who genuinely understand D-numbers — crew chiefs, Goodyear engineers, and the three teams at each tire test — are exactly the people barred from betting on it. So the information is public, causally central, and structurally orphaned: nobody who can price it holds it, and nobody who holds it can price it.
- **Information lead:** Three separate leads. (1) Hard calendar lead: the Goodyear release lands Tuesday or Wednesday for a Sunday race, while outright markets were posted Sunday night off last week's result and most matchup and prop markets fill out Wednesday through Friday — 24 to 72 hours of live pricing against a spec you already have. (2) Physical-discovery lead: the field itself does not learn how the compound behaves until first practice on Saturday, and the market's entire tire-adaptation signal is Saturday practice/qualifying speed. Betting Wednesday puts you 72–96 hours ahead of the mechanism by which the price eventually corrects. (3) Structural lead, the biggest one: the tire-test roster is published weeks to months ahead — the Iowa test was announced May 11 for an August 7–9 race, an 88-day lead — and the cross-track D-number panel exists nowhere, so neither is ever priced at all, not late, not ever. The lead there is not measured in hours; the information simply never arrives at the line.
- **Why still under-exploited:** The codes are published as prose inside press releases syndicated to Jayski, Speedway Digest and NASCAR.com — never as structured data, never with an API, never archived by any results database. Reconstructing the panel means crawling a decade-plus of weekly wire posts and regexing four-digit D-numbers out of sentences: manual, unglamorous, and worth nothing unless you already believe compound beats track-type as a similarity key. No vendor sells it; there is no Kpler or Ortex of NASCAR rubber, because NASCAR is far too small a betting market for a quant shop to staff. The sport's own public data products all inherited the track-type ontology and never revisited it. And the window is unusually open right now: the option-tire program (2024–) and the 2026 750-hp/short-track aero package at five venues have broken the historical track priors that the market is still leaning on, while simultaneously multiplying the number of never-before-run codes — the exact races where the tire-test monopoly is worth the most.
- **Rough +EV:** The screen fires on roughly 15–22 Cup races per year (new right-side code, changed construction, option-tire allotment, or a code returning from a physically dissimilar track), yielding ~6–12 tradeable matchups each, plus a parallel book in Xfinity/Truck — call it 150–250 wagers annually. Break-even on -110 matchups is 52.4%; a realistic target is 54–56%, i.e. 3–7% ROI per bet. The subset with real teeth is the brand-new-code races (~6–8 per season), where top-10 props on tire-test organizations priced +150 to +300 may be 8–15 percentage points underpriced — those are the wagers that carry the year. Practical ceiling is set by limits, not by edge: NASCAR matchup and prop limits run roughly $500–$2,000, so a single operator should expect $4k–$18k of annual profit on $75k–$200k of turnover, scaling only by adding books and the lower series. This is a genuine edge in a small pond, not a capacity trade.
- **Confidence:** Medium. Biggest uncertainty is statistical power and confounding: the Next Gen car dates only to 2022, so the clean panel is ~4.5 seasons × 36 Cup races, and the specific cell that matters — "same D-number recurs at a physically dissimilar track" — may hold only a few dozen observations, which is thin for estimating a driver-level effect. Worse, the tire changes are entangled with simultaneous aero and horsepower package changes (2024 short-track package, 2026 750-hp at five venues), so a naive backtest will happily attribute package effects to compound. The honest failure mode: once you control for organization speed and recent form, the cross-track D-number key adds nothing beyond track type, and the whole idea collapses back to the much narrower but still real tire-test-monopoly subset — six to eight races a year, three organizations each. Before staking, backfill the panel and test whether same-code cross-track residuals beat same-track-type residuals out of sample; if they do not, bet only the new-code/test-roster leg and size it small.
