## 81. The Tray Ledger

**Arena:** gambling — cricket totals markets (T20 franchise leagues, associate/ICC events, and T20Is at new or rebuilt grounds)
**Domain:** VENUE PHYSICS AND GROUNDS CHANGES. RULES: institutions only; sanctioned collection

- **Data source:** A hand-built provenance registry of cricket playing surfaces: individual drop-in pitch trays (soil batch, nursery, grow-in days, prior venue, realized scoring history), square-relay dates, and outfield systems/suppliers — assembled from the public board packets and council agendas of the government bodies that own most of these grounds, plus turf-contractor and venue-authority disclosures, calibrated against the ICC's published Pitch & Outfield ratings. The load-bearing, obscure fact: a cricket pitch is a physical ~2.5m x 25m soil block, and drop-in trays are re-used and trucked between venues. The two trays that produced the notorious sub-100 first innings at the 2024 T20 World Cup in Nassau County were dug up and hauled ~2,900 miles to the Oakland Coliseum for MLC 2025. Scoring behaviour is a property of a specific movable object, not of a venue's postcode — and nobody keeps a ledger of the objects.
- **How to collect it:** Four fragmented, sanctioned institutional streams, all pullable by one person:
(1) Public venue-authority board packets — Oakland–Alameda County Coliseum Authority posts full board packages as PDFs (theoaklandarena.com/about-us/coliseum-authority/meetings, e.g. /assets/doc/Board-Package-9.19.25-*.pdf) and agendas via Granicus (oakland.granicus.com/boards); the cricket conversion, including the plan to truck the New York trays in and crane them into the infield, was presented to this board before any public schedule existed.
(2) City/county legislative records for the (mostly publicly owned) grounds — City of Grand Prairie TX council agendas/minutes (15-year ground lease + $1.3M city contribution for the AirHogs-to-cricket conversion, approved unanimously in open council); Nassau County NY Legislature and Dept. of Parks contract items for Eisenhower Park; Broward County Commission agendas for Central Broward Park, Lauderhill; UK borough planning portals plus the PlanIt aggregator for outfield/drainage works at county grounds.
(3) Turf-contractor and venue newsrooms naming the physical asset and its timeline — adelaideoval.com.au/news (Adelaide Oval Turf Solutions grows and maintains the trays), tencategrass.us/newsroom, LandTek Group project pages, STRI reports.
(4) Ground truth / calibration — ICC Pitch & Outfield ratings (icc-cricket.com/about/cricket/rules-and-regulations/pitch-ratings) and icc-cricket.com/media-releases, which publish a per-venue rating and demerit points for every Test/ODI/T20I; joined to ESPNcricinfo ball-by-ball to compute each tray's realized first-innings distribution, boundary %, and run-rate-by-over curve.
- **The bet / trade:** Cricket totals, same-day settlement, placed at market open (T-3 to T-7 days) when books are still on a league-generic venue prior. Primary: UNDER first-innings team total and UNDER match aggregate runs for the first 1-4 matches played on a newly installed or relocated drop-in square whose tray lineage has a documented low-scoring/variable-bounce history. Secondary: UNDER total fours + sixes (boundary-count props) when the outfield has also been freshly relaid in natural turf (slow, long-cut, moisture-holding). Reverse the sign — OVER on boundary counts and aggregate — when a tired natural outfield is replaced with a new fast synthetic/sand-carpet system, which is disclosed by the supplier. Exit at settlement; optionally scale in-play on Betfair through the first six overs if the surface reads slow.
- **Mechanism:** Pace, bounce and carry off a cricket pitch are set by the soil's clay content, consolidation (rolling hours) and root maturity. A relocated or newly grown tray is under-consolidated with immature roots: the ball sits up, bounce turns variable, stroke-play timing collapses, and run rates fall 20-40%. Simultaneously, a newly laid outfield is slow — balls that would run to the rope stop for two — and boundary percentage is the single largest term in a T20 total. Both inputs are set by a physical construction event with a known date, months before the first ball. Because the tray is a transportable object, its measured scoring distribution at venue A is a far better prior for venue B than venue B's own (nonexistent) history — which is exactly the substitution no bookmaker's venue model makes.
- **Who's on the other side:** Bookmakers pricing a venue with zero or near-zero match history fall back to a league-average prior (MLC first innings ~180-190; ICC T20 WC ~160) and only re-anchor after one to three matches of realized data. The 2024 Nassau case is the clean demonstration: opening totals sat near the tournament prior while the first innings came in at 77, 96 and 119, and the venue averaged 107 across the event. On the other side of the under sits the structural recreational over-bias in cricket totals — casual money buys sixes. Cricket analytics vendors (CricViz and similar) model pitch behaviour retrospectively from ball-tracking after the match; none maintain a forward-looking registry of tray provenance, grow-in days, or municipal groundworks, because the inputs are municipal PDFs and turf-contractor press rooms in four countries rather than a feed anyone sells.
- **Information lead:** Two to nine months on the construction event, versus a market that first sees the surface at the toss. Grand Prairie's conversion cleared city council roughly 2.5 years before the first MLC ball. The Oakland tray transfer surfaced in a public JPA board presentation before the fixture list. Turf-contractor and venue-authority posts give the tray extraction, transport and grow-in dates weeks before installation. Books post venue-specific totals 3-7 days out and materially re-price only after match 1-2 has been played — so the actionable window is the opening line on match 1 through roughly match 4, with the largest single edge on match 1.
- **Why still under-exploited:** There is no product. The inputs are a JPA board packet PDF, a Texas city council minute, a Nassau County parks contract, an Adelaide turf company's news page and a Dutch turf manufacturer's US newsroom — four jurisdictions, no API, no aggregator, and nothing that looks like sports data. The core insight (that drop-in pitch trays are re-used, migrating physical assets that carry their scoring behaviour with them across a continent) is essentially unremarked outside curator circles. The affected competitions — MLC, ILT20, CPL, associate internationals, brand-new Indian/African/Olympic venues — sit below the attention threshold of the syndicates that grind IPL and international cricket. And unlike tennis court pace, which has been fully productized in the last two years (public Court Pace Index databases and published betting-adjustment guides now exist), cricket surface provenance has no equivalent.
- **Rough +EV:** Calibration case (Nassau 2024): effective mispricing of 40-70 runs on first-innings and aggregate lines, worth well over 30% on the under for the first two matches — an outlier, not the base rate. Steady state: roughly 20-40 qualifying surface events per year globally (new venues, relocated trays, relaid squares and outfields across MLC, ILT20, CPL, The Hundred expansion grounds, associate internationals, new Indian and Southern African venues, plus the LA 2028 build-out), each yielding 1-4 tradeable matches. Modeled edge ~5-12% on matches 1-2, decaying to ~2-3% by match 4, on lines priced near -110/-115. Practical limits of $500-$3k per side on franchise and associate cricket totals imply roughly $20-70k/yr expected profit for a small team, with meaningful upside via Betfair in-play scaling and via correlated boundary-count props, which are softer and less limited than the main total.
- **Confidence:** Medium. Biggest uncertainty is sign stability: "new surface" does not reliably mean "low scoring." A well-cured tray on a fast-draining base can play as a batting road, and curators actively remediate between matches — the ICC ordered work on the Nassau square mid-tournament and scoring rose, and MLC's own grounds staff bedded the same trays in for a month before Oakland with the explicit aim of making them bat better. The edge therefore depends on tray-specific provenance and grow-in days, not a blanket new-equals-under rule, which means the registry must be genuinely good or the trade is a coin flip with vig. Secondary risk: after the 2024 New York embarrassment, some books now flag brand-new venues and open more conservatively, compressing the match-1 edge.

## 82. The March 18 Cohort

**Arena:** financial-market
**Domain:** RULE AND REGIME CHANGES that create new populations (the Cold-Air Bleeder archetype). RULES: institutions only; sanctioned collection

- **Data source:** SEC Forms 3/4/5 filed by directors and officers of foreign private issuers (FPIs) — a class of filer that did not exist before March 18, 2026. The Holding Foreign Insiders Accountable Act (folded into the FY2026 NDAA, signed Dec 2025) repealed Rule 3a12-3(b), which had exempted FPIs from Section 16(a) since 1935. As of 2026-03-18, every officer and director of a US-listed FPI must report open-market trades on EDGAR within 2 business days. The SEC's March 5 and May 22, 2026 exemptive orders carve out only individuals already covered by qualifying home-country regimes in six jurisdictions (Canada, Chile, EEA, Korea, Switzerland, UK), leaving a large non-exempt residue: Cayman/BVI-incorporated China ADRs, Marshall Islands/Bermuda shipping, Israel, Japan, Taiwan, Brazil, Mexico, Colombia, India, Turkey, Kazakhstan. Verified empirically: Form 3 filings spiked to 8,297 index rows on 2026-03-18 vs ~160 on a normal day (2026-02-18) — roughly 4,000 new insiders across ~640-900 issuers registering in a single session. Costamare Inc. (Marshall Islands, CIK 1503584) has zero Forms 3/4/5 in EDGAR history until five Form 3s dated exactly 2026-03-18, then Form 4s on 3/30, 7/2 and 7/30. Ongoing flow measured over six sessions in Aug 2026: ~200 Form 4s from the new cohort (~33/day, ~7,500/yr) from names like Luckin Coffee, Kaspi.kz, Adagene, Yatra Online, Karooooo, Lion Group, Silicom, Banco Santander Brasil, Grupo Cibest, Costamare Bulkers. Critically, Sections 16(b) and 16(c) still do NOT apply to FPI insiders — no short-swing disgorgement, no short-sale ban.
- **How to collect it:** All free and sanctioned. (1) Real-time: EDGAR current-events Atom feed https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcurrent&type=4&output=atom, polled every few minutes. (2) Daily: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/daily-index/{YYYY}/QTR{n}/form.{YYYYMMDD}.idx — Form 4 rows are indexed by issuer CIK. (3) Each filing is structured XML (ownershipDocument) with transaction code, date, price, share count, and the officer/director flags. (4) Universe construction is trivially exact: pull the 2026-03-18 daily index, take every issuer CIK with a Form 3 that day, and confirm via https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK##########.json that no Form 3/4/5 exists before that date — "first-ever Form 3 dated 2026-03-18" IS the membership test for the new population. The same JSON carries stateOfIncorporation (1T = Marshall Islands, E9 = Cayman, etc.) to strip out the six exempt jurisdictions. (5) ADS-to-ordinary ratios (needed or every position size is off by 2-40x) come from each issuer's F-6 registration statement on EDGAR or the depositary bank's ADR page (BNY Mellon adrbnymellon.com, Citi, JPM, Deutsche). (6) For the cross-market leg, the home-country disclosure calendars are public too: Brazil CVM open data (dados.cvm.gov.br, Resolution 44 monthly consolidated insider file), Taiwan MOPS monthly insider holdings filings, Mexico BMV/EMISNET, India NSE/BSE SAST-PIT disclosures. A one-person setup: ~200 lines of Python, an EDGAR poller, and a spreadsheet of ADS ratios.
- **The bet / trade:** Systematic long basket in US-listed FPI equities on insider cluster-buy signals from the non-exempt cohort. Signal: >=2 distinct officers/directors of the same issuer file open-market purchases (transaction code P only — exclude A awards and M option exercises) within a rolling 30 days, aggregate >$150k or >10% increase in reported holdings, at an issuer whose first-ever Form 3 is dated 2026-03-18. Buy on filing day, equal-weight, hold 3-6 months, monthly rebalance, hedge beta with a short in EEM/ACWX or a sector ETF so you own the idiosyncratic signal. Skew allocation toward the smallest, least-covered names (China/Cayman smid-caps, Marshall Islands shipping, Israeli and LatAm smid) where information asymmetry is widest. Mirror sleeve: avoid or short-into-strength names with >=2 opportunistic insider sales (code S, non-plan, non-vest-adjacent). Second, higher-lead variant for the dual-listed subset (Brazil, Taiwan, Mexico, Colombia, India): on an EDGAR cluster-buy signal, buy the HOME-market ordinary/unit line — usually 5-20x more liquid than the ADR — within hours of the filing, and hold through the scheduled home-country insider disclosure date (e.g. CVM's consolidated report on the 10th of the following month), a 1-5 week event with a fixed catalyst.
- **Mechanism:** Insider purchases predict returns most strongly where public information is thinnest. FPIs are the thinnest information environment on a US exchange: they file a 20-F annually and 6-Ks at their discretion — no 10-Q, no quarterly guidance, often no earnings call, sparse analyst coverage, and material local-language disclosure. The gap between what management knows and what the tape knows is therefore structurally larger at an FPI than at any domestic issuer. Until March 18, 2026 that gap was completely invisible: for a Cayman-incorporated China ADR or a Marshall Islands shipowner there was no insider disclosure anywhere on Earth — not in the US, not in the (nonexistent) home regime. The statute converts that invisible channel into a 2-business-day public feed. Three amplifiers make the raw signal unusually clean: (a) Section 16(b) short-swing disgorgement and 16(c) short-sale prohibition were deliberately NOT extended, so FPI insiders trade without the six-month holding penalty that shapes US insider behavior — their trades are opportunistic by construction; (b) FPIs have no 10b5-1 plan culture and no quarterly blackout calendar, because they have no quarters — so the trades are not laundered into pre-scheduled programs the way ~60% of US insider volume is; (c) with no quarterly reporting, an insider buying in month 4 of a 6-month reporting gap is acting on information the market genuinely cannot see for months. Directionally: cluster purchases front-run positive news that will surface at the next 6-K or 20-F; the price reaction is currently muted because almost nobody screens this subset, so the drift is slow rather than instantaneous.
- **Who's on the other side:** Three groups, each slow for a different structural reason. (1) Home-market investors. A São Paulo, Taipei, Mexico City or Mumbai institution monitors its own regulator (CVM/RAD, MOPS, EMISNET, NSE) and its local data vendor (Economatica, Quantum). None of them ingest EDGAR ownership XML, because until five months ago there was nothing in it for their names. They will learn of a Brazilian director's purchase from CVM's consolidated monthly file on the 10th of the following month. (2) The US insider-alpha industry. VerityData/InsiderScore, Washington Service, 2iQ, Quiver, OpenInsider, Finviz and the Bloomberg insider screens were all built on the domestic Section 16 universe — FPIs were legally impossible to include before March 2026, so none of them have a single day of history. Systematic funds cannot allocate to an unbacktestable signal; the usual internal bar is 2-3 years of out-of-sample data, which puts real quant capital in 2028-2029. (3) Anyone running a naive screen. The 2026-03-18 avalanche (8,297 Form 3 rows in one day, 50x normal) buries the signal in initial-ownership noise for months, and the ADS-ratio problem means a parser that treats Form 4 "shares" as ADS mis-sizes every China ADR and Japanese megabank by 2-40x. Foreign name transliteration and translated officer titles break the standard entity-resolution pipelines. That engineering friction is exactly what buys a small team its window.
- **Information lead:** Two distinct leads. Against the home market it is mechanical and measurable: Brazilian insiders report to the issuer within 5 days, and CVM publishes only a consolidated monthly disclosure by the 10th of the following month — so a Form 4 hitting EDGAR at T+2 business days beats Brazilian public disclosure by roughly 1 to 5 weeks depending on where in the month the trade falls. Taiwan's MOPS monthly insider filings give a similar 1-4 week lead; Mexico, Colombia and India are days to weeks. Against the US tape the lead is not calendar time but attention: domestic Form 4s are priced within hours by a dozen commercial screens, whereas the FPI cohort currently has no dedicated screener, so the same filing sits unread and the drift plays out over weeks instead of a day. And for the Cayman/BVI/Marshall Islands subset — China ADRs and Greek-controlled shipping — the lead against the prior state of the world is unbounded: this information did not exist in any jurisdiction before 2026-03-18, so the only competition is other people reading the same EDGAR feed, and there are very few of them right now. The window closes when the vendors ship FPI coverage; call it 18-36 months.
- **Why still under-exploited:** The dataset is five months old and has exactly zero pre-history — that single fact is why it is under-exploited, and it is not a fact anyone can engineer around. Systematic capital requires backtests; there is nothing to backtest until roughly 2028. Every commercial insider-data product on the market was architected around a domestic-issuer universe because FPI insider data was legally nonexistent, so adding it is not a config change but a coverage build (ADS ratio normalization, foreign entity resolution, translated titles, multi-currency, home-market line mapping). The rule itself was a legislative rider inside a defense authorization bill rather than an SEC rulemaking, so it got law-firm client alerts and essentially no buy-side attention; there was no comment period to telegraph it to quant shops. The March 18 Form 3 flood actively poisons naive screens. The exemption structure is individual rather than issuer-level and jurisdiction-dependent, so building the correct universe requires reading two SEC exemptive orders and mapping EDGAR state-of-incorporation codes — friction that filters out casual replication. And the genuinely novel leg — using a US regulatory filing to trade the São Paulo or Taipei line ahead of local disclosure — requires someone who simultaneously watches EDGAR and a foreign regulator's publication calendar. Almost nobody sits in that intersection. Finally, capacity is small: many of these names trade $1-20m/day, so this is a $5-50m strategy, which is precisely the size that large funds ignore and keeps it alive.
- **Rough +EV:** Base rate from the literature on opportunistic (non-routine) insider purchases: ~0.5-0.8%/month abnormal return (Cohen-Malloy-Pomorski ~0.55%/mo), rising to 1-1.5%/mo for cluster buys in small, low-analyst-coverage names; Jeng-Metrick-Zeckhauser put purchase portfolios near 6%/yr. The FPI cohort should sit at or above the top of that range for four structural reasons — semiannual reporting maximizes the asymmetry, no 16(b)/16(c) constraint means trades are unlaundered and opportunistic, coverage is minimal, and there is no competing arbitrageur base. Working estimate: 8-15% annualized gross alpha on the hedged cluster-buy long book in the first 12-24 months, decaying toward the domestic 3-5% by 2028-2029 as vendors ship coverage. Fire rate: ~33 cohort Form 4s per trading day (~7,500/yr); open-market purchases are typically 10-15% of Form 4 volume, and the >=2-insider cluster filter should yield roughly 150-350 events/yr, i.e. 3-7 actionable long signals per week — enough for a 40-80 name rotating book. The dual-listed home-line variant is rarer and sharper: perhaps 15-30 high-conviction trades/yr with a scheduled catalyst, where a 3-6% move over a 2-5 week hold is a reasonable target. Costs: ADR borrow on small China names is expensive and often unavailable, so run it long-biased with index hedges rather than paired shorts; home-line execution adds FX and foreign-investor registration friction that can eat 50-150bp per round trip in Brazil, Taiwan and India.
- **Confidence:** Medium. The data source, the rule change, the population, and the collection path are all verified hard facts — I confirmed the Form 3 flood (8,297 rows on 2026-03-18 vs ~160 on a normal day), the 640+ issuer universe, Costamare's zero-then-March-18 filing history, and ~200 cohort Form 4s over six recent sessions. What is NOT verified is the payoff, and that is the biggest uncertainty: only five months of post-compliance data exist, so nobody — including me — has established that FPI insider purchases actually predict returns rather than being mechanically noisy. Much of the March-June flow is one-off Form 3 cleanup, restricted-share vesting mis-tagged as purchases, and ADS-ratio artifacts. The first job for a small team is to run the March 18 - August 2026 sample and measure the 1/3/6-month abnormal returns to cluster buys before committing capital; if the drift is already same-day, the edge is gone before it starts. Second-order risks: a chilling effect where FPI insiders simply stop trading in the open market, and the 10%-beneficial-owner carve-out (controlling families and sponsor vehicles remain fully exempt) meaning the most informed holders at many of these issuers still never file — which shrinks the sample and could bias it toward less-informed management trades.

## 83. The 71-Depot Tape

**Arena:** financial-market
**Domain:** STATE-REGISTERED PRODUCTION LEDGERS (the Roe Window archetype). RULES: institutions only; sanctioned collection

- **Data source:** The Karnataka State Beverages Corporation Ltd (KSBCL) daily and monthly "supplier-wise / depot-wise" sales ledgers of IML (Indian Made Liquor) and beer, in CASES — plus the sibling state-monopoly ledgers of Kerala BEVCO, Tamil Nadu TASMAC, Andhra Pradesh APSBCL and Telangana TGBCL. KSBCL is the statutory sole wholesaler in Karnataka: every legal case of spirits and beer sold in the state is issued through its 71 IML depots and recorded, and the corporation publishes the issuance ledger publicly at daily frequency. This is a company-level (supplier-level) unit-volume ledger for a market where no scanner panel legally exists.
- **How to collect it:** Verified live as of 2026: KSBCL daily sales index at https://ksbcl.karnataka.gov.in/113/daily-sales-report/en — each day posts an .xls under epoch-stamped, opaque filenames (e.g. /uploads/media_to_upload1770009709.xls = "Daily IML-Beer Sales 31.01.2026"; ...1769662974.xls = 27.01.2026; ...1767591085.xls = 03.01.2026). Monthly reports are the "Supplierwisedepotwisesales" series (legacy archive: ksbcl.com/ksbcl_monthlysalesreport.html and www.ksbcl.com/pgMonthlySalesforKSBCL.htm; legacy daily pattern www.ksbcl.com/DAILY_SALES_REPORTS/DD_MM_YYYY.xls). SKU→supplier→listed-parent mapping comes from the supplier-wise item-wise price list (ksbcl.karnataka.gov.in/uploads/media_to_upload1727334746.pdf) and stateexcise.karnataka.gov.in IMFL slab notifications. Companion feeds: bevco.in/sales-details/ (Kerala), tasmac.co.in, apsbcl.ap.gov.in, tsbcl.nic.in and data.telangana.gov.in. Build: a nightly cron that scrapes the index page (filenames are non-deterministic, so you must harvest the listing, not guess URLs), stores every .xls, and normalizes supplier names. Requires Indian/residential egress — the .gov.in host rate-limits and 503s foreign datacenter IPs (it blocked my proxy). Critically, nothing is archived: the legacy public archive dead-ends in 2017, so the panel exists only for whoever started collecting.
- **The bet / trade:** Event trade into Indian alcobev quarterly results. Build a supplier-level case-volume panel for the quarter, compare to consensus volume growth, and take a directional position entered T-10 to T-2 trading days before the results date, exited results-day +1. Core names: United Breweries (NSE: UNITDBRD) and United Spirits (NSE: UNITDSPR) — both have liquid single-stock futures/options, so the short leg is executable — with Radico Khaitan (RADICO), Allied Blenders (ABDL) and Tilaknagar Industries (TI) traded long-only or as the long leg of a pair against the alcobev basket. Second, larger-payoff overlay: on any state Additional Excise Duty / MRP notification (Karnataka has issued four beer AED hikes in under two years, plus a March 2026 policy revamp), measure the realized volume elasticity from the daily depot tape over the following 15-20 trading days and hold the implied direction 4-8 weeks — the market prices the headline instantly but cannot price the elasticity until results.
- **Mechanism:** Alcohol is a State subject in India, so each state monopoly wholesaler is a mandatory chokepoint: supplier ships to depot, depot issues to retail, both legs are logged. Karnataka is ~12-15% of national volumes for both United Breweries and United Spirits (some sell-side estimates put it near 20% of USL's IMFL volume) and ~5-7% for Radico, Allied Blenders and Tilaknagar; Karnataka + Kerala + Tamil Nadu + Andhra + Telangana together are roughly 45-58% of all IMFL sales. For these companies, price is administered and published in advance (excise slabs, MRP notifications) and input costs (ENA, glass, barley) are trackable — so the residual earnings surprise is almost entirely VOLUME. A supplier-wise case count from the depot ledger therefore reads the revenue line directly, weeks before it prints. The 2025 Karnataka episode is the proof: beer volumes collapsed 19.55% (195.27 lakh boxes through September 2025, 47.46 lakh fewer than prior year) after successive AED hikes to 200%, while UBL's stock ground down 15% from February as the market slowly discovered what the depot tape already knew day by day.
- **Who's on the other side:** Domestic retail and long-only mutual funds, who own Indian alcobev heavily and trade it as a premiumisation story; domestic sell-side, which models monthly state EXCISE REVENUE in rupees from finance-department releases — a number that conflates duty hikes, MRP resets and mix shift with actual cases, and is exactly the wrong series when the policy variable is moving; and global consumer funds that mark United Spirits off Diageo's group commentary. They are slow for structural reasons, not lazy ones: there is no national alcohol volume statistic in India because alcohol is a state subject, and Nielsen/Kantar retail panels exclude alcohol in India, so the scanner shortcut that exists in every other consumer category simply does not exist here. The only counter is the state corporations themselves, and reading them means five separate portals in four formats, some in Kannada/Telugu/Tamil, with rotating ephemeral filenames and no history.
- **Information lead:** The full quarter's Karnataka case volumes are in hand roughly one day after quarter-end, because the ledger is daily. United Breweries, United Spirits and Radico report quarterly results ~30-50 days after quarter-end. So the lead is about 4-7 weeks on 12-20% of the volume base — and it is a running nowcast, meaning two-thirds of the quarter is known a month BEFORE the quarter even closes. On excise-shock elasticity the lead is larger and cleaner: the volume response is legible 2-3 weeks after a duty notification, versus roughly three months for the market. Local press does occasionally leak a lagged state aggregate ("beer sales down 19.55% through September"), but never supplier-wise and never at daily frequency, so even that leak is a coarse, delayed shadow of the tape.
- **Why still under-exploited:** The scraping vendors that already touch these portals (e.g. WebDataInsights, which explicitly lists TASMAC, BEVCO, PLCB, LCBO) sell PRICE lists, excise-duty components and government-fixed rates — not case volumes. There is no NABCA equivalent, no Nielsen coverage, no packaged Indian liquor volume panel. The data is genuinely hostile to collect: epoch-stamped filenames that cannot be enumerated, a .gov.in host that blocks foreign datacenter IPs, per-state formats, and above all no archive — the historical series is destroyed continuously, so the asset can only be manufactured by someone who has been running a daily harvester. Foreign funds cannot get at it; domestic funds have the access but default to the rupee excise-revenue series because it arrives pre-aggregated in a press release. That combination — a mandatory, complete, company-level unit ledger sitting behind a scraping problem nobody has bothered to solve — is why it is still open.
- **Rough +EV:** Indian alcobev results produce a 1-day absolute move averaging ~4-8%, with fat tails (Tilaknagar +14% on Q4 FY25; UBL -15% over a quarter on Karnataka duty drag). If a supplier-level case panel covering 15-45% of a company's volume base lifts sign-accuracy on the 1-day move from 50% to a plausible 62-65%, gross edge is ~0.5-1.2% of notional per event. About 20 events/year across five names, plus 3-6 excise-policy elasticity setups where the payoff is much larger (5-15% on a single name over 4-8 weeks). Gross ~12-25%/yr on the sleeve; net of Indian STT, 30-60bp round-trip in the midcaps, and the constraint that only USL/UBL/RADICO have usable F&O for the short leg, call it ~5-12% net annualized. Capacity is the binding limit — TI and ABDL are thin, so this is a few-$mm strategy, not a few-hundred-$mm one.
- **Confidence:** Medium. Biggest uncertainty: whether the CURRENTLY published daily .xls is genuinely supplier-wise (company-attributable) or only depot-wise category totals. The legacy monthly series is explicitly labelled "Supplierwisedepotwisesales" and KSBCL separately publishes a supplier-wise item-wise price list, which strongly implies company-level detail persists — but the live 2026 file could not be opened from here because the .gov.in host 503s non-Indian egress, so this is inference, not inspection. Verify by pulling one file from an Indian IP before building anything. If it turns out to be depot-only, the edge degrades from stock-specific to a category call (beer vs IMFL, sector-level), which is still tradable but roughly halves the EV. Secondary risks: depot issuance diverges from company primary sales when channel inventory swings (though that divergence is itself a channel-stuffing signal), and Karnataka's March 2026 excise policy revamp can break historical elasticity mappings mid-sample.

## 84. The Establishment Delta

**Arena:** financial-market
**Domain:** EMBARGOED OR RESTRICTED-DISTRIBUTION DATA obtainable another lawful way (the Embargoed Sounding archetype). RULES: sanctioned/lawful collection only — own sensors or public receipt, never system intrusion

- **Data source:** The "Establishment" block inside FDA/NLM Structured Product Labeling (SPL) — the per-NDC list of every physical site involved in making a US drug, with site name, DUNS/FEI, address, and NCI operation codes (API MANUFACTURE C84731, MANUFACTURE C43360, ANALYSIS, STERILIZE, PACK, LABEL), which 21 CFR 207 compels every labeler to file. Contract-manufacturing relationships are the single most tightly-held commercial secret in pharma (CDMOs are contractually barred from naming customers; sell-side gets nothing from management), and the datasets that map them — Clarivate Cortellis CMO, GlobalData PharmSource, Redica — are expensive, curated from press releases, sold to pharma sourcing/QA rather than investors, and publish no time series. The drug-listing statute forces the same relationships into a free public XML feed. The novel step is not looking one up; it is snapshotting the whole corpus daily and running it as a differenced panel: a dated, machine-readable ledger of who makes what for whom, and who just stopped.
- **How to collect it:** All free, no auth, no vendor. (1) DailyMed bulk SPL: dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/spl-resources-all-drug-labels.cfm — full-release zips (~150k SPLs) plus daily/weekly update zips. Parse HL7v3: author/assignedEntity/representedOrganization = registrant; each assignedEntity/assignedOrganization carries <id root="1.3.6.1.4.1.519.1"> (DUNS), performance/actDefinition/code (operation), and manufacturedMaterialKind/id (the specific NDC that site touches). (2) DECRS, the Drug Establishments Current Registration Site, updated every business day — bulk via healthdata.gov Socrata dataset s52i-rmqw — gives FEI↔DUNS↔address↔registration status; FDA's FEI Search Portal (free account) closes address gaps. (3) openFDA /drug/ndc.json and /drug/drugsfda.json to walk NDC→application→marketer→molecule→dosage form. (4) Event joins, all FEI- or address-keyed: Import Alert 66-40 Red List (accessdata.fda.gov/cms_ia/importalert_189.html), the weekly Inspection Classification Database, Warning Letters, EudraGMDP statements of GMP non-compliance (eudragmdp.ema.europa.eu), and the FDA/ASHP shortage lists. Critical operational point: DailyMed serves only the CURRENT label. There is no published history of establishment blocks, so the delta panel does not exist until you start accruing it — a cron job, a few hundred GB, and patience are the entire moat.
- **The bet / trade:** Primary: a monthly "defection index" = count of US NDCs whose MANUFACTURE or API MANUFACTURE establishment resolves to a PRC-domiciled DUNS (WuXi AppTec 2359.HK, WuXi Biologics 2269.HK, WuXi XDC 2268.HK, Asymchem, Porton, Hangzhou/Shanghai sites). When the 3-month delta turns decisively negative, short WuXi Biologics + WuXi AppTec against long Samsung Biologics (207940.KS) and Lonza (LONN.SW); when it is flat or positive — which is the actual state through most of 2025-26 — take the reverse and fade the BIOSECURE panic. Hold 1-2 quarters, exiting into WuXi semiannual results (March/August) or the January 1260H list update. Overlay, 10-30x/yr, 5-60 day holds: on every new Import Alert 66-40 Red List add, EU statement of non-compliance, or CGMP warning letter, use the graph to short the non-obvious US-listed NDC marketers whose product is made at that site (AMRX, TEVA, VTRS, PRGO, HIK.L) — usually not the site owner, so not the name that already moved — and go long the sole surviving registered supplier of the affected molecules (ANIP, AMPH, HIK.L). Third leg: track establishment additions on the GLP-1 SPLs (Wegovy/Ozempic/Zepbound/Mounjaro) as a dated read on fill-finish capacity coming online, traded against NVO and LLY over weeks-to-quarters.
- **Mechanism:** A drug cannot legally ship from a site that is not listed against its NDC, and the listing must be updated when the arrangement changes (plus recertified in the June and December listing windows and at annual registration renewal Oct-Dec). So a site appearing on a label is a legally-compelled receipt that a supply contract was signed and qualified; a site disappearing is a receipt that it was terminated or replaced. Chain one: WuXi's revenue is customer contracts → contracts terminate → the site drops off US labels → 2-4 quarters later it shows up as a revenue/backlog miss. The label change is the earliest hard evidence, and it precedes both the announcement and the accounting. Chain two: FDA hits a site → every NDC listing that site is at supply risk → the site owner's stock reprices within minutes because the news names the owner, but the downstream US marketers who merely buy from it are never named, and the molecules that go into shortage (and therefore whose surviving supplier gets pricing power) are not identified for days or weeks. The graph resolves both instantly because the site→NDC→marketer→molecule edges are already public. Chain three: injectable capacity is the binding constraint on GLP-1 volume; a new fill-finish establishment appearing on the label is the moment capacity became legally usable, not the moment management chooses to discuss it.
- **Who's on the other side:** CDMO analysts, who model off disclosed backlog and "N-1/N+" project counts and have no independent customer-level view because the contracts are confidential. Generalists trading the BIOSECURE/1260H headline flow — the December 2025 NDAA version dropped the named-entity list, WuXi AppTec was then proposed for the January 2026 1260H update, and the complex has swung 20-40% on political text while nobody measured whether customers were actually leaving. On the event overlay, specialty pharma analysts who correctly short the site owner but cannot answer "who else is exposed" because contract-manufacturer relationships appear nowhere in a 10-K. They are slow for structural reasons: this is 150k+ HL7v3 XML documents keyed on DUNS (not FEI, not CIK, not ticker), requiring a fuzzy DUNS/FEI/address crosswalk against a separate daily-refreshed registration file; the establishment block is universally treated as compliance boilerplate; and the historical panel simply is not for sale — even the vendors who map supply chains sell a curated current-state picture to procurement departments, not a differenced series to investors.
- **Information lead:** CDMO leg: the SPL edit lands when the arrangement changes and is force-refreshed each June and December, roughly 2-4 quarters before the lost volume shows in a CDMO's reported revenue and 1-2 quarters before sell-side channel checks surface it; WuXi reports only semiannually, so the worst case is a ~6-month lead and the typical case is longer. Event overlay: the second-order exposure map is available the same minute the Red List page changes, versus 1-10 days for the market to work out downstream marketers and frequently never for the shortage-beneficiary leg. Regulatory pre-warning: an EU statement of non-compliance in EudraGMDP for a site typically posts weeks-to-months before the corresponding FDA action, and Red List additions have themselves been running weeks ahead of the public warning letter — so the site-level watchlist fires before the tradeable event. GLP-1 leg: an establishment addition predates management commentary on supply by a quarter or more.
- **Why still under-exploited:** Four compounding reasons. (1) No history exists to buy: DailyMed exposes only the current label, so the delta series — the entire signal — must be self-accrued daily and cannot be backfilled from any vendor. Whoever started snapshotting owns it. (2) The data is misclassified: establishment blocks are read by QA and regulatory-affairs staff as a filing obligation, never by markets as economics; FDA itself has publicly conceded it cannot map the US drug supply chain well from its own registration data. (3) The commercial substitutes point the wrong way — Redica, Cortellis CMO, GlobalData PharmSource sell curated, announcement-derived, current-state supply-chain maps at high cost to pharma sourcing teams; none is a market-data product and none publishes a defection rate. (4) The question that makes the series valuable is brand new: BIOSECURE only became law in December 2025 via the FY2026 NDAA with the named-entity list stripped out, pushing everything onto the January 1260H update — so "are customers actually leaving WuXi, and how fast" became the dominant CDMO question in 2026, and it happens to be exactly and only measurable from label listings. Legally this is clean: it is a free federal publication, no scraping of restricted systems, no confidential information, no duty owed to anyone.
- **Rough +EV:** Event overlay is the reliable engine: roughly 30-60 site-level actions a year touch US-marketed drugs; maybe 15-25 have a listed-company second-order exposure that is not already obvious from the headline. Assume a 5-10% move in the exposed marketer, capture 2-4% net of slippage on perhaps half — call it 8-12 winning events/yr at ~3%. The sole-surviving-supplier leg is rarer but fatter: 3-6 a year at 5-20% (shortage-driven pricing is why ANIP/AMPH re-rate). CDMO pair: 2-4 material repricings a year with ±20-40% amplitude; knowing the true defection rate should be worth 5-15pp per event on the pair, and the highest-value trade is the fade — being long the complex into a scary 1260H headline because the labels show no exodus. Blended, on dedicated capital this plausibly runs mid-single to low-double-digit annualized with a fat right tail from 2-3 events. Capacity is the binding constraint, not edge: HK/KRX/SIX lines plus mid-cap US specialty pharma caps this at maybe $20-50mm before you move the names, which is precisely why it survives.
- **Confidence:** Medium. Biggest uncertainty by a distance: listing hygiene. Labelers routinely leave defunct sites on labels for months and add "qualified but unused" alternate sites for redundancy, so a listing change is a noisy proxy for a volume change — you must require corroboration (a drop paired with an add on the same NDC on the same date, restricted to MANUFACTURE/API MANUFACTURE ops, weighted by the marketer's revenue in that molecule) and expect a meaningful false-positive rate in the first year while you calibrate. Second, and specific to the CDMO leg: US commercial NDC listings capture only commercial-stage manufacturing, missing the clinical/development and non-US book that is a large share of WuXi's revenue, so the index is a partial read that could stay flat while the actual business erodes at the pipeline end. Third, DUNS→FEI→corporate-parent resolution is genuinely messy at the site level and is where most of the engineering time will go. The event overlay is the higher-confidence half; the CDMO pair is the higher-payoff, lower-confidence half.

## 85. The Dime Clock

**Arena:** financial-market
**Domain:** CONSEQUENCE-FUNCTION CHANGES where the hazard changes but behavior doesn't (the Beaching Ratio archetype). RULES: institutions only; sanctioned collection

- **Data source:** The per-security consecutive-day count of Nasdaq **official closing BID price ≤ $0.10** — the countdown clock created by Nasdaq's "Modified Low-Price Requirement" (SR-NASDAQ-2025-065, SEC-approved Dec 5, 2025, effective **January 19, 2026**). The rule: if a Nasdaq-listed security's *closing bid* is $0.10 or less for **ten consecutive trading days**, Nasdaq **must** issue a Staff Delisting Determination, the company is **ineligible for any compliance period**, and a Hearings Panel appeal **does not stay the trading suspension** — the stock is suspended to OTC while it appeals. Layered on top: the Jan 2025 amendment barring any compliance period for a company that effected a reverse split within the prior 12 months, and the pending MVLS-under-$5M immediate-suspension standard. Nobody publishes the streak counter. It has to be constructed daily from four fragmented public feeds.
- **How to collect it:** Four sanctioned institutional sources, joined nightly: (1) **True closing bid** — the load-bearing field. Not available in Yahoo/TradingView/most retail APIs, which carry *last sale*. Pull NBBO/Nasdaq official closing quote from Polygon.io (`/v3/quotes/{ticker}`, ~$29–199/mo), Databento (Nasdaq TotalView/BBO), Alpaca, or Nasdaq Basic. Because Reg NMS Rule 612 permits sub-penny quoting below $1.00, a name can print a $0.1010 last sale on a $0.0987 closing bid — the clock runs invisibly on consumer charts. (2) **Nasdaq Non-Compliant Company List** — https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/stocks/non-compliant-company-list, free, daily, CSV download, ~100 names, with a distinct "penny stock non-compliant" bucket; gives existing bid-price deficiencies and notification dates. (3) **Nasdaq Trader Equity Corporate Actions Alerts** — https://www.nasdaqtrader.com/Trader.aspx?id=archiveheadlines&cat_id=105, free, public, no login (e.g. ECA2026-325, ECA2026-19); every reverse split with CUSIP change, giving the prior-12-month reverse-split disqualifier. (4) **SEC EDGAR full-text search** (efts.sec.gov, free) for 8-K **Item 3.01** filings and DEF 14A / 8-K Item 5.07 — the latter tells you whether shareholders have *already authorized* a reverse split, which is the single best rescue-risk filter. Item 3.01 is the lagging confirmation you are trading ahead of.
- **The bet / trade:** **Short the common stock** of Nasdaq-listed names at day 5–7 of a ≤$0.10 closing-bid streak. Qualifying filter: closing bid ≤ $0.07 (cannot realistically reset above $0.10 without a corporate action) AND at least one of — already on the non-compliant list for bid price; effected a reverse split within the prior 12 months (no compliance period available); no shareholder-authorized reverse split outstanding per the latest DEF 14A/Item 5.07. **Horizon: 5–25 trading days.** Cover on the 8-K Item 3.01 print, on Nasdaq's suspension notice, or hard-stop on two consecutive closes with a bid above $0.10. Secondary expression where a chain exists (usually names that recently reverse-split and fell back): short-dated OTM puts. Tertiary, slower leg: **fade the post-reverse-split drift** over 20–60 trading days on names that just spent their one allowed reverse split — the split no longer resets the clock, it burns the last life.
- **Mechanism:** A death-spiral-financed Nasdaq microcap has an ATM or equity-line agent selling stock continuously into the bid — a mechanically price-insensitive seller that walks the quote down through $0.10. Pre-2026, that was survivable: 180 days grace, a second 180 days, then a reverse split, clock reset. The entire microcap ecosystem is built on that hazard function. As of Jan 19, 2026 the hazard collapsed from ~360 days to **10 trading days**, and the appeal no longer keeps you on the exchange. Three behaviors did not change. (a) Issuers keep running the same dilution program that drives the bid under a dime. (b) Boards still schedule reverse splits on the old corporate calendar — proxy, special meeting, effectiveness is a 60–90 day process, so a board that files a DEF 14A when the stock is at $0.12 now gets suspended before the meeting is held; the remedy is structurally slower than the trigger. (c) Retail keeps running the "buy the sub-$1 name, wait for the reverse split, ride the pop" playbook that was correct for fifteen years. Once the determination lands, the security is suspended to OTC — losing marginability, losing buy-side access at Robinhood/Webull/Fidelity, losing index and ETF membership, and often landing on the Expert Market where no public quotes display at all. Realized declines from determination through suspension run -35% to -85%.
- **Who's on the other side:** Retail microcap traders running the pre-2026 compliance-play script (StockTwits/Reddit/Discord "it always reverse-splits and bounces"), plus small market-makers pricing delisting risk off base rates fitted on pre-2026 data where the modal outcome was survival. Behind them, the handful of delisting-arb desks that trade the 8-K Item 3.01 — they are structurally 8–11 trading days late by construction, because the 8-K is due four business days *after* a letter that is itself issued after day 10. Index and ETF holders (Russell Microcap, broad total-market funds) can only sell at actual delisting, so they are forced sellers into your cover. They are slow for four compounding reasons: the rule is seven months old and buried in an SRO approval order; the trigger is on closing *bid*, a field almost no retail data feed carries; counting consecutive-day streaks requires maintaining a daily panel nobody maintains; and the whole tradable universe is too small for anyone who could afford proper data to bother.
- **Information lead:** Detection at streak day 5–6. Nasdaq's determination letter is mandatory at day 10 and issued within roughly 1–3 business days. The 8-K Item 3.01 is due within 4 business days of the letter, landing around day 14–17 of the streak — that is when the tape learns. So **~8–11 trading days ahead of the 8-K, and ~15–25 trading days ahead of the actual suspension**. Against an observer using last-sale data only, the lead is effectively unbounded: they may never realize the clock started, because sub-penny quoting lets a $0.098 closing bid coexist with $0.101 last-sale prints all week.
- **Why still under-exploited:** The rule went live January 19, 2026 — there is no historical base rate anyone has fitted, because the pre-2026 sample has the opposite hazard function. No commercial vendor sells a "days-until-mandatory-delisting-determination" counter; Kpler/Vortexa are commodity flow, YipitData/M Science are consumer transaction, Ortex is short interest — none of them touch exchange listing mechanics. The signal requires joining four ugly, unglamorous public sources (an ASPX table, a corporate-actions headline archive, EDGAR full text, and a paid quote feed), and the payoff universe is sub-$50M market caps that no institution with that data budget can deploy into. That mismatch — the data is cheap but the capacity is tiny — is precisely why the inefficiency survives. The closing-bid-vs-last-sale wrinkle is the second moat: it is a genuine data-plumbing detail that filters out everyone working from free charts.
- **Rough +EV:** Signal frequency: roughly 4–10 qualified entries per month (typically 15–40 Nasdaq commons sit under a $0.10 closing bid at any time, clustered). Hit rate ~65–75%. Median winner -35% to -55% from a day-6 entry to suspension; losers are reverse-split or financing pops of +40% to +200%, so the payoff is negatively skewed and per-name sizing must be hard-capped. Gross expectancy ~+10% to +18% per fired signal. Frictions: borrow 30–200% annualized over a ~3-week hold costs 2–11%; sub-penny spreads are surprisingly benign at 0.5–3%. **Net roughly +5% to +12% per fired signal**, 5–8 signals a month, capacity ~$50k–$300k gross per name. Very high return on a small book, uninvestable above a few million dollars — that capacity ceiling is the honest headline, not the percentage.
- **Confidence:** Medium-high on the mechanism, medium on realized EV. The rule text, the effective date, the closing-bid trigger, the no-stay suspension and all four data feeds are verified and public. The single biggest uncertainty is **locate availability** — these are exactly the names where borrow is unobtainable at any price, and an unfillable short is a zero-EV signal no matter how good the forecast. Second uncertainty is the reverse-split rescue tail: a company with pre-existing shareholder authorization can effect a split in days and torch the position, which is why the DEF 14A / Item 5.07 authorization check is not optional, and why the ≤$0.07 bid filter (reset requires a corporate action, not a pump) does most of the risk work.

## 86. The Phantom Home Leg

**Arena:** gambling
**Domain:** SCHEDULING AND TRAVEL BURDEN visible in published calendars. RULES: institutions only; sanctioned collection

- **Data source:** Displaced-venue designations in official UEFA and club-published match calendars, converted into actual door-to-door transit itineraries. Since 2022 (Ukraine) and late 2023 (Israel), a growing set of clubs play their nominal HOME European matches in a third country, while continuing to play domestic matches at home. Every data feed and every public model records these as "home" fixtures with the displaced venue's coordinates — which is a badly wrong proxy for the real burden. Concrete confirmed cases for 2026-27: Dynamo Kyiv's European home matches at Arena Lublin, Poland (announced on fcdynamo.com); Shakhtar Donetsk at Stadion Miejski im. Henryka Reymana, Kraków (announced on shakhtar.com); Hapoel Beersheba hosting in Szombathely, Hungary; Beitar Jerusalem's "home" leg in Ploiesti, Romania. Ukrainian airspace has been fully closed since Feb 2022, so Ukrainian clubs reach their own "home" ground by an ~18-hour overland journey from the Kyiv training base to Kraków (press reporting puts a Kraków–Kyiv–London European round trip at ~36 hours of cross-border bus transit). The adjacent, same-mechanism source is extreme-distance participation: Kairat Almaty's 2025-26 Champions League campaign covered ~44,800 km with a record 6,908 km single leg to Lisbon and 3+ time zones each way, while the Kazakhstan Premier League runs concurrently. None of this — border-crossing bus hours, closed-airspace routing, zero real home crowd at a "home" match — exists as a field in any commercial feed.
- **How to collect it:** (1) Venue + date + kickoff from UEFA's official competition match calendars at uefa.com (published within 24-72h of each draw; 2026-27 CL league-phase draw is Thu 27 Aug 2026, Nyon, with MD1 on 8-10 Sep 2026), cross-checked against club press releases which announce the displaced ground weeks earlier (shakhtar.com/en/news, fcdynamo.com/en/news, club sites for Israeli entrants). (2) Domestic fixture lists and kickoff times, including in-season reschedules: upl.ua/en/tournaments/games for the Ukrainian Premier League, football.org.il for Ligat ha'Al, pfl.kz for the Kazakhstan Premier League, plus the UEFA national-association domestic pages (uefa.com/nationalassociations/ukr|isr). (3) Turn each fixture pair into a real itinerary: OSRM/OpenStreetMap road routing from the club's actual training base to the operative border crossing and onward airport (Rzeszów/Kraków/Warsaw for Ukrainian clubs; Chișinău as the southern route), plus great-circle distance and time-zone delta for flown legs. Produce per-fixture features: total transit hours, number of border crossings, time zones crossed, hours of recovery between final whistle and next domestic kickoff, and a binary "nominal home match at a foreign ground" flag. (4) Prices and line history: Pinnacle's odds pages/API for the thin leagues, oddsportal.com/football/ukraine/premier-league and the Israel/Kazakhstan equivalents for closing-line archives, footystats.org for backfill. All of it is public, institution-published, and scrapeable within normal terms of use.
- **The bet / trade:** Two linked single-match bets, both settling at 90 minutes on the day of the match. (A) DISPLACED-HOME FADE: in UEFA qualifying/league-phase matches where the nominal home club is playing at a third-country venue it had to cross a border to reach, back the visiting side on the Asian handicap (typically taking +0.25 to +0.75 depending on price) — i.e. fade the phantom home advantage. (B) THE SPILLOVER FADE, the higher-edge leg because the market is thinner: in any Ukrainian Premier League, Ligat ha'Al or Kazakhstan Premier League fixture falling within 96 hours after a European match whose computed one-way transit exceeds ~12 hours or 3 time zones, fade the European participant — back the domestic opponent on the Asian handicap, or take the participant's team-total UNDER. Place 48-72 hours out at Pinnacle/SBOBet/Asian books, before lineups post. Season overlay: within 72 hours of the 27-28 Aug 2026 draws, price the full-season burden map and take domestic outright/points-handicap positions (UPL top-2, Kazakh title) against clubs whose burden is unusually front-loaded, held to season end in May 2027.
- **Mechanism:** Physical recovery and travel load degrade sprint distance, high-intensity actions and late-game defensive concentration; that part is uncontroversial sports science and is the same engine behind the known "Thursday-night hangover." What is different here is magnitude and invisibility. A Premier League club's European home match costs zero travel; Shakhtar's costs roughly 36 hours of round-trip surface transit through a border crossing, because Ukrainian airspace is closed and the "home" ground is 1,000+ km away in another country. Then the squad must make the same journey in reverse to play a domestic league match three or four days later, sometimes in Kyiv and sometimes in the far west of the country — so the burden varies fixture to fixture in a way that is fully computable from published calendars and completely absent from any feed. Second channel: home advantage itself. Books apply a standard home coefficient to the nominal home side. At a displaced ground the club has no home crowd (several of these have been ordered behind closed doors), no familiar pitch, and has traveled further than its opponent — the sign of the travel asymmetry is literally inverted versus what the model assumes. Neutral-venue research puts the home-advantage loss at roughly 10-20% of the effect; here you get that loss stacked on top of a negative travel differential. Third channel: rotation and squad depth. A club burning 36 hours of transit per European tie rotates harder domestically, and in a thin league the market prices the badge, not the eleven.
- **Who's on the other side:** Bookmakers pricing Ukrainian, Israeli, Kazakh, Azerbaijani and Caucasus domestic leagues, and the recreational money in those markets. These leagues are priced off Elo/consensus engines with a small feature set — form, home/away flag, rest days, sometimes venue coordinates — and the desks that build genuinely bespoke models allocate that effort to the big five leagues where the handle is. The soft books copy Pinnacle; Pinnacle's originators are not hand-modeling Shakhtar's bus route. Domestic recreational money is overwhelmingly one-directional on the dominant club (Shakhtar, Dynamo, Maccabi Tel Aviv, Kairat), which pushes the line further past fair. Crucially, the two most plausible sophisticated competitors are blind in the same way: (i) fatigue/travel datasets built from match-venue coordinates see "Shakhtar, home, Kraków" as one short hop and "Maccabi Tel Aviv, home" as zero travel; (ii) the academic and blog literature on European-hangover effects is trained on Western European clubs where the effect is an order of magnitude smaller, so the coefficient anyone imports is far too small for this population.
- **Information lead:** Two distinct leads. Identification lead: displaced venues are announced by the clubs themselves — Dynamo confirmed Arena Lublin and Shakhtar confirmed Kraków via their own newsrooms — typically one to several weeks before the venue propagates into UEFA's public calendar and into odds-provider fixture data. Then, within 24-72 hours of the 27-28 Aug 2026 draws, you hold the complete season map of every high-burden fixture pair through May 2027, while books do not open prices on individual UPL/Ligat ha'Al/Kazakh matches until roughly 3-7 days out — an identification lead of one to five months per fixture. Pricing lead: this is not a decaying informational lead, it is a permanently missing feature. The transit-hours variable is never incorporated, so the edge is available at the open AND survives into the close, except to the extent it leaks through published lineups about an hour before kickoff. Practically, the exploitable window is from line open (T-7d) to lineup release (T-1h), with the cleanest entry at T-72h to T-48h when limits are lower but the price is rawest.
- **Why still under-exploited:** It is a regime that only came into existence in 2022 and expanded in late 2023, so there is essentially no historical training data and no vendor has built the feature. It cannot be derived from any feed anyone sells: you have to know that a "home" match is at a foreign ground, that the club's airspace is closed, and that the squad therefore travels by road to a border crossing — facts that live in Ukrainian- and Hebrew-language club press releases, not in Opta/Sportradar fixture objects. It is fragmented across four or five national federation sites in four languages plus UEFA plus club newsrooms, and the venue assignments change season to season and sometimes mid-season. The leagues involved carry low handle, so nobody with a budget has bothered. And the one adjacent thing that IS well known — the generic "Europa League hangover" — actively conceals it, because anyone who has already "handled" European fatigue with a Western-European-calibrated coefficient believes the box is ticked. The public discussion of neutral venues that exists is generic betting-forum chatter about crowd effects; nobody is routing buses.
- **Rough +EV:** Roughly 60-100 qualifying fixtures per season across UPL, Ligat ha'Al, the Kazakhstan Premier League and Azerbaijani/Caucasus entrants, of which perhaps 25-40 are high-conviction (transit >20h or a displaced home leg immediately followed by a long domestic trip). Estimated true effect: displaced "home" status is worth ~0.15-0.35 goals less than the applied home coefficient, and the post-transit domestic fixture ~0.10-0.25 goals. Against Asian handicap lines priced at roughly -105 to -108 with no such feature, that maps to about a 2-5% ROI, hit rate only a few points above break-even, high variance — expect a realistic chance of a losing season on 30 bets. Throughput is the binding constraint: Pinnacle/SBOBet limits on these leagues run roughly $300-1,500 at T-72h, rising toward $2,000-5,000 near kickoff, so ~$60-200k of turnover per season implies ~$2-8k expected profit standalone. The honest framing is that this is a strong FACTOR rather than a standalone business — its real value is as an un-priced regressor inside a broader thin-league model, or as a filter that turns marginal plays into clear ones.
- **Confidence:** Medium. The data source is verified real and genuinely unmodeled, and the mechanism is sound. The biggest uncertainty is the rotation confound: Shakhtar, Dynamo, Maccabi Tel Aviv and Kairat are so dominant domestically that they often win comfortably with a rotated eleven, and rotation is precisely the channel through which fatigue would show up — but rotation becomes visible to the market via published lineups about an hour before kickoff, which is exactly when the closing line forms. So the open question is whether a residual survives after controlling for lineup strength, or whether the whole effect is already impounded by team news. That is testable: four completed seasons of the displaced regime (2022-23 through 2025-26) plus Kairat's 2025-26 campaign give enough fixtures to fit the residual, and if it does not survive the lineup control, the idea collapses to the pre-lineup window only, which is also where the limits are smallest. Secondary risks: UEFA could restore Israeli hosting rights (the IFA has been lobbying for exactly that) or the Ukrainian regime could end, killing the population; and small-league lines can be sharp for idiosyncratic local reasons that have nothing to do with travel.

## 87. The Selection Item

**Arena:** gambling — combat-sports proposition markets (world-title boxing and UFC championship bouts held in Nevada)
**Domain:** OFFICIATING AND ADJUDICATION PATTERNS from published assignment data. RULES: officials as assigned institutions, published statistics only; sanctioned collection

- **Data source:** Nevada State Athletic Commission public meeting agendas and minutes, specifically the "F. NEW BUSINESS" line items reading "Selection of officials and setting of fees to work [DATE] at [VENUE] for [TITLE] between [A] and [B], for possible action." Nevada statute requires the Commission to vote on and name the referee plus three judges for every championship and special-event bout in the state — and Nevada hosts the plurality of world-title boxing and UFC numbered-event title fights. This is joined to two volunteer-run per-official scoring archives: BoxRec judge pages (boxrec.com/en/judge/{id}, fight-by-fight scorecards going back decades) and MMADecisions.com per-judge pages plus its "Minority Report" (how often a judge dissents from the other two) and "10-10 Report" (even-round propensity). Verified live: the 02-18-26 agenda seated officials for five title bouts including Fundora–Thurman on March 28 and Opetaia–Glanton on March 8.
- **How to collect it:** (1) Scrape the agenda archive monthly at the stable URL pattern https://boxing.nv.gov/uploadedFiles/boxingnvgov/content/schedule/{YY}_Agendas/{MM-DD-YY}-AG.pdf — I pulled 26_Agendas/02-18-26-AG.pdf and parsed it with pypdf; regex on "Selection of officials" yields bout, event date, venue, and sanctioning body. (2) Capture the official NAMES at the meeting itself: the agenda prints a public call-in number (1-775-321-6111, Conference ID 500 653 951) and the vote names the referee and three judges bout by bout; confirm afterward against the minutes PDF posted to the same year folder. (3) Build per-official priors by scraping BoxRec judge pages and MMADecisions.com per-judge pages, the Minority Report, and the 10-10 Report. (4) Add fighter style covariates free from UFCStats.com (significant strikes, takedowns, control time) and BoxRec/CompuBox for boxing. (5) Enlarge the training sample using post-event officials PDFs published by California CSAC (dca.ca.gov/csac/events/results/) and Texas TDLR, which list the assigned referee and judges for every completed bout.
- **The bet / trade:** Method-of-victory props on the specific commission-assigned title bouts, entered 1-5 weeks before the fight and held to settlement at the final bell. Two separable legs: (a) REFEREE leg — "Fight goes the distance" Yes/No, or total rounds over/under, taking the side favored by the assigned referee's stoppage-threshold history; (b) JUDGE-PANEL leg — "Fighter X to win by decision" (typically +250 to +600), taking the fighter whose stylistic profile matches the assigned panel's documented criteria weighting. Convex tertiary: the boxing DRAW prop (+1500 to +3000) when the seated panel has an elevated even-card/114-114 history. Bet the decision prop, never the moneyline — the prop isolates P(win | goes to cards), which is the only quantity the officials assignment moves.
- **Mechanism:** The Commission's vote fixes four named humans who jointly determine the outcome of any non-finish. Referees vary measurably and persistently in stoppage threshold and in how long they let a hurt fighter continue (and in MMA, how fast they stand fighters up from guard), which directly shifts the probability the bout reaches the final bell — the entire distance leg. Judges vary in criteria weighting under genuinely ambiguous rules: the Unified Rules and the boxing 10-point-must system never specify whether volume/aggression/control-time outranks damage/clean punching/ring generalship, so each judge resolves the ambiguity the same way every time. Sal D'Amato has repeatedly awarded rounds to the fighter with fewer significant strikes; Chris Lee has dissented from the other two judges 37 times. In a stylistically polarized matchup — pressure fighter vs. boxer, wrestler vs. striker — swapping one aggression-weighting judge for one damage-weighting judge moves P(A wins | decision) by several points, and swapping two moves it a lot. Books construct method-of-victory prices mechanically as P(distance) x P(A wins | distance), setting the conditional roughly equal to the unconditional moneyline adjusted for the two fighters' career finish rates. There is no officials term anywhere in that model, so the assignment is not merely learned late — it is never priced.
- **Who's on the other side:** Sportsbook prop traders and the small combat-sports syndicates that shape UFC/boxing props. They are structurally slow for five reasons. (1) The data lives in a state consumer-affairs agency's meeting minutes, not in any sports feed — Sportradar and Genius carry no pre-event combat-sports officials. (2) Prop desks auto-derive method-of-victory from the moneyline and finish rates; adding an officials covariate would require a model rebuild for a low-headcount, low-handle vertical relative to NFL/NBA. (3) The counterparty history data sits on two hobbyist archives (BoxRec, MMADecisions) with no API and messy name disambiguation. (4) The informed public frames judging as random noise — "robbery," "fire Sal D'Amato" — rather than as a stable, estimable per-official parameter, so even sharp money treats it as unforecastable. (5) Books that do move on officials news react only to the handful of UFC title assignments that MMA Junkie and Sherdog write up, which is a small subset of what the Commission actually seats each month.
- **Information lead:** Verified concretely from the Feb 18, 2026 agenda: officials were seated for bouts 3 days out (Feb 21, T-Mobile), 18 days out (March 8, UFC Apex), and 38 days out (March 28, MGM Grand). So the referee and judge panel for a world title fight are publicly determined typically 2-5 weeks before the bout, occasionally more. Against combat-sports media the lead is hours to a couple of days — the names are spoken live on the public teleconference and only a minority of assignments (mostly UFC title fights) ever get written up, usually the next day. Against the sportsbook the lead is effectively permanent: since the officials never enter the method-of-victory model, you are not merely early, you are the only participant pricing the input. That also means the edge does not decay as the fight approaches — it persists until the opening bell.
- **Why still under-exploited:** Nothing commercial covers it. Legal/regulatory analytics vendors do not track state athletic commissions; sports data vendors do not carry combat-sports officials pre-event; there is no "Ortex for judges." The pipeline is deliberately unpleasant: monthly PDF scraping of a Nevada state agency archive, dialing into or streaming a public commission meeting to capture names before minutes post, scraping two volunteer-run sites with inconsistent name spelling, and joining all of it to fighter style features. Each step is easy; the composite is exactly the fragmented, manual work that keeps a source under-exploited. The qualitative version is common bar-talk, but the quantitative panel-composition-conditional version aimed at a market with zero officials term is not a product anyone sells. There is also a genuinely fresh regime break: the Association of Boxing Commissions issued an MMA Scoring Criteria Clarification in July 2025 elevating impact/damage over volume and control time, which is re-forming judge behavior right now — priors are being rewritten this season, and no book has modeled the transition.
- **Rough +EV:** NSAC seats officials for roughly 60-120 championship/special-event bouts a year; maybe 40-70 carry liquid method-of-victory props. You should only fire when the panel sits at a tail AND the matchup is stylistically polarized, which realistically qualifies 15-25 bets/year. Sizing the edge honestly: the referee leg plausibly moves P(goes the distance) by 2-5 points on a ~45-55% base, which clears a 5-8% prop hold only at referee extremes. The judge leg is bigger — in a clear stylistic mismatch with a skewed panel, P(A wins | decision) can move 4-10 points, and on a "by decision" prop at +250 to +600 a 5-point probability shift is a 15-35% EV swing on that leg. Blended expectation is roughly +6% to +12% ROI per qualifying bet with very high variance; at $2k average stake that is about $2k-$6k/year — hobby scale, but genuinely positive. The draw leg is the convex tail: title-boxing draws run ~3-4%, and an elevated-even-card panel plausibly runs 5-7%; at +2000 that takes EV from about -37% to about +15%, firing maybe 3-6 times a year. Scaling requires extending the same pipeline to fight-night officials sheets for non-title bouts (a 2-6 hour lead but ~500 UFC fights/year of volume).
- **Confidence:** Medium. Biggest uncertainty by far: whether per-judge scoring tendency has enough out-of-sample reliability to deliver the 4-10 point conditional-winner shift the EV assumes. Judges accumulate only 20-60 scored decisions each, and assignment is emphatically NOT random — the Commission hands marquee bouts to senior judges — so a naive per-judge win-rate is badly confounded with the fights they happened to draw. Identification requires a paired design: score each judge against the other two on the same bout, and against the MMADecisions media-consensus card, with fight fixed effects. If the cleanly identified judge effect comes in under ~3 points, prop juice eats the entire edge and the idea is dead. Secondary risks: prop limits on non-marquee title fights run $500-$2k, capping scale; and a bettor who only ever takes method-of-victory props on Nevada title fights is a trivially obvious pattern that books will limit within a season, so the position has to be laundered across markets or spread across multiple accounts and exchanges.
